# Overview



![NicheCompass Logo](https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/nichecompass/blob/main/docs/_static/nichecompass_logo_readme.png)

**NicheCompass** (Niche Identification based on Cellular grapH Embeddings of COMmunication Programs Aligned across Spatial Samples) is a comprehensive Python package for end-to-end analysis of spatial multi-omics data. Designed for spatial transcriptomics and spatial proteomics workflows, NicheCompass enables researchers to identify and characterize cellular niches, integrate multiple spatial samples, and perform spatial reference mapping across datasets [README.md](https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/nichecompass/blob/main/README.md#L11-L11).

## What is NicheCompass?

NicheCompass is a deep learning framework built on graph neural networks that leverages gene programs—coordinated sets of genes involved in specific biological processes—to understand cellular interactions in spatially resolved data. The framework combines prior knowledge from biological databases with data-driven discovery through de novo gene program extraction, enabling both interpretable and exploratory analysis of spatial tissue organization [docs/index.md](https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/nichecompass/blob/main/docs/index.md#L3-L4).

The core innovation is the **Variational Gene Program Graph Autoencoder (VGPGAE)**, a specialized neural architecture that learns low-dimensional latent representations of cells while simultaneously reconstructing both gene expression patterns and spatial connectivity patterns. This dual-reconstruction approach captures the complex interplay between cellular state and spatial context [src/nichecompass/modules/vgpgae.py](https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/nichecompass/blob/main/src/nichecompass/modules/vgpgae.py#L1-L4).

## Core Architecture

NicheCompass implements a sophisticated modular architecture designed for flexibility and scalability in spatial omics analysis.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input Layer"
        A[AnnData Object<br/>Spatial Transcriptomics] --> B[Gene Expression Matrix]
        A --> C[Spatial Coordinates]
        A --> D[Gene Programs<br/>Prior + De Novo]
        A --> E[Optional ATAC-seq Data]
    end

    subgraph "VGPGAE Module"
        B --> F[Graph Construction<br/>KNN Connectivity]
        F --> G[Encoder<br/>GATv2/GCNConv]
        G --> H[Latent Space<br/>Gene Program Activations]
        H --> I[RNA Decoder]
        H --> J[Edge Decoder]
        E --> K[Chromatin Decoder]
    end

    subgraph "Output Layer"
        I --> L[Reconstructed Expression]
        J --> M[Reconstructed Connectivity]
        K --> N[Accessibility Reconstruction]
        H --> O[Latent Representations]
    end

    subgraph "Analysis Layer"
        O --> P[Niche Identification]
        L --> Q[GP Importance Analysis]
        M --> R[Cell-Cell Communication]
        P --> S[Spatial Atlas Building]
    end

    style A fill:#e1f5ff
    style H fill:#fff4e1
    style P fill:#f0f0f0
    style Q fill:#f0f0f0
    style R fill:#f0f0f0
```

The architecture processes spatial data through several key stages: graph construction from spatial coordinates, encoding via graph neural networks, latent representation learning through gene program activations, and dual reconstruction of both expression patterns and spatial relationships [src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py](https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/nichecompass/blob/main/src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L24-L248).

> [!TIP]
> The encoder supports both GCNConv (Graph Convolutional Network) and GATv2Conv (Graph Attention Network v2) layers, with GATv2Conv recommended for most applications as it learns attention weights that highlight the most important neighbors for each cell [docs/user_guide/index.md](https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/nichecompass/blob/main/docs/user_guide/index.md#L13-L13).

## Key Features and Capabilities

NicheCompass provides a comprehensive suite of tools for spatial omics analysis, ranging from basic data processing to advanced analytical capabilities.

### Spatial Analysis Workflows

The framework supports three primary analysis paradigms tailored to different experimental designs:

| Workflow Type | Description | Use Case | Tutorial |
|--------------|-------------|----------|----------|
| **Single-Sample Analysis** | Process one spatial sample independently | Initial exploration, pilot studies | [mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb](https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/nichecompass/blob/main/docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb) |
| **Sample Integration** | Combine multiple samples into spatial atlas | Multi-slide studies, tissue atlases | [mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb](https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/nichecompass/blob/main/docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb) |
| **Spatial Reference Mapping** | Map new samples to existing reference | Clinical applications, cross-study comparison | [mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb](https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/nichecompass/blob/main/docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb) |

### Multi-Modal Support

Beyond standard RNA-based spatial transcriptomics, NicheCompass supports joint modeling of RNA and ATAC-seq (Assay for Transposase-Accessible Chromatin) data, enabling researchers to link chromatin accessibility patterns with gene expression in spatial contexts [docs/index.md](https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/nichecompass/blob/main/docs/index.md#L3-L4).

The multimodal tutorial provides guidance on working with paired data, which is particularly valuable for understanding regulatory mechanisms in spatial tissue organization [mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb](https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/nichecompass/blob/main/docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb).

### Gene Program Analysis

Gene programs are the conceptual core of NicheCompass, representing coordinated gene sets that drive specific biological processes. The framework supports two types:

- **Prior Gene Programs**: Curated from biological databases (e.g., MSigDB, GO, KEGG) based on known biology
- **De Novo Gene Programs**: Discovered from the data through unsupervised learning, capturing novel patterns [src/nichecompass/utils/gene_programs.py](https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/nichecompass/blob/main/src/nichecompass/utils/gene_programs.py)

The package provides comprehensive tools for gene program analysis including importance scoring, differential testing, and biological interpretation [src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py](https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/nichecompass/blob/main/src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L1053-L1056).

## Project Structure

The NicheCompass codebase is organized into six main packages, each handling specific aspects of the analysis pipeline.

```
src/nichecompass/
├── data/                 # Data loading and preprocessing
│   ├── dataloaders.py    # PyTorch Geometric dataloaders
│   ├── dataprocessors.py # Data transformation utilities
│   ├── datareaders.py    # File format readers
│   └── datasets.py       # Dataset classes
├── models/               # Model definitions and training
│   ├── nichecompass.py   # Main NicheCompass model class
│   └── utils.py          # Model utilities
├── modules/              # Neural network modules
│   ├── vgpgae.py         # VGPGAE implementation
│   └── losses.py         # Loss function definitions
├── nn/                   # Neural network components
│   ├── encoders.py       # Graph encoder architectures
│   ├── decoders.py       # Graph decoder architectures
│   ├── layers.py         # Custom layer implementations
│   └── aggregators.py    # Node label aggregators
├── train/                # Training infrastructure
│   ├── trainer.py        # Training loop implementation
│   └── metrics.py        # Evaluation metrics
└── utils/                # Analysis utilities
    ├── analysis.py       # Niche characterization tools
    ├── gene_programs.py  # GP management functions
    └── multimodal_mapping.py # Cross-modal mapping
```

The data package handles AnnData integration and graph construction, the models package provides the high-level training interface, the modules package contains the core VGPGAE neural network, the nn package implements specific graph neural network components, the train package manages the training process, and the utils package provides downstream analysis capabilities [src/nichecompass/__init__.py](https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/nichecompass/blob/main/src/nichecompass/__init__.py#L3-L5).

## User API Overview

NicheCompass provides a streamlined user API centered around the `NicheCompass` model class, which integrates analysis capabilities directly into the model interface for ease of use [docs/api/user.md](https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/nichecompass/blob/main/docs/api/user.md#L31-L41).

### Core Methods

| Method | Purpose | Output |
|--------|---------|--------|
| `train()` | Train the VGPGAE model on spatial data | Trained model with latent representations |
| `get_latent_representation()` | Extract learned cell embeddings | Low-dimensional latent coordinates |
| `run_differential_gp_tests()` | Identify differentially active gene programs | Statistical test results |
| `compute_gp_gene_importances()` | Score gene importance for specific GPs | Ranked gene importance scores |
| `get_neighbor_importances()` | Analyze cell-cell communication | Neighborhood attention weights |
| `get_gp_summary()` | Get overview of all gene programs | Summary DataFrame |

The API is designed to be intuitive for users familiar with single-cell analysis tools like Scanpy, with methods following similar naming conventions and return patterns [docs/api/user.md](https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/nichecompass/blob/main/docs/api/user.md#L31-L41).

> [!TIP]
> All analysis results are stored directly in the AnnData object using standardized keys prefixed with `nichecompass_`, ensuring seamless integration with downstream single-cell analysis workflows and facilitating reproducible analyses [src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py](https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/nichecompass/blob/main/src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L194-L221).

## System Requirements

NicheCompass requires Python 3.10 and recommends GPU support for training, particularly for larger datasets. The package has been tested on CUDA-enabled GPUs but does not yet support Apple silicon or multi-GPU training [docs/installation.md](https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/nichecompass/blob/main/docs/installation.md#L3-L5).

Installation requires several external dependencies including PyTorch, PyTorch Geometric libraries, and bedtools (for ATAC-seq integration) [docs/installation.md](https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/nichecompass/blob/main/docs/installation.md#L25-L32).

## Documentation Structure

The NicheCompass documentation is organized into four main sections:

- **Get Started**: Installation and quick-start guides
- **Tutorials**: Step-by-step examples for different analysis workflows
- **User Guide**: Best practices and hyperparameter recommendations
- **API Reference**: Detailed documentation of all functions and classes

Each section builds upon the previous ones, providing a progressive learning path from initial installation to advanced usage [docs/index.md](https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/nichecompass/blob/main/docs/index.md#L6-L50).

## Getting Started with NicheCompass

To begin using NicheCompass, you should follow this recommended learning path:

1. **Install and Setup**: Configure your environment with required dependencies [Installation and Setup](3-installation-and-setup)
2. **Quick Start**: Run a simple example to understand the workflow [Quick Start](2-quick-start)
3. **Learn Architecture**: Understand the VGPGAE model and design principles [NicheCompass Model Architecture and Core Concepts](4-nichecompass-model-architecture-and-core-concepts)
4. **Explore Tutorials**: Work through hands-on examples matching your analysis needs
5. **Deep Dive**: Consult specialized documentation for specific analysis techniques

The user guide provides valuable hyperparameter recommendations based on ablation experiments, helping you optimize model performance for your specific dataset and biological question [docs/user_guide/index.md](https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/nichecompass/blob/main/docs/user_guide/index.md#L3-L14).

# Quick Start



Get up and running with NicheCompass in minutes. This guide walks you through the essential workflow for analyzing spatial multi-omics data, from installation to your first analysis.

![NicheCompass Logo](https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/nichecompass/blob/main/docs/_static/nichecompass_logo_readme.png)

NicheCompass (**N**iche **I**dentification based on **C**ellular grap**H** **E**mbeddings of **COM**munication **P**rograms **A**ligned across **S**patial **S**amples) enables end-to-end analysis of spatial multi-omics data including spatial atlas building, niche identification & characterization.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L1-L10), [index.md](docs/index.md#L1-L10)

## What You'll Learn

This Quick Start covers the complete NicheCompass workflow:
- Installing required dependencies
- Preparing spatial data with gene programs
- Training the NicheCompass model
- Performing initial analysis

By the end, you'll understand the core architecture and be ready to explore advanced features in the full tutorials.

Sources: [mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb#L10-L25)

## Architecture Overview

NicheCompass uses a Variational Gene Program Graph Autoencoder (VGPGAE) architecture that integrates spatial information with biological prior knowledge through gene programs.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Spatial Data<br/>AnnData object] --> B[Spatial Graph<br/>KNN neighbors]
    B --> C[NicheCompass Model<br/>VGPGAE]
    
    D[Gene Programs<br/>Prior Knowledge] --> C
    
    C --> E[Latent Representation<br/>GP embeddings]
    C --> F[Reconstruction<br/>Gene expression]
    C --> G[Reconstruction<br/>Spatial edges]
    
    E --> H[Analysis Outputs]
    H --> I[Niche Identification]
    H --> J[GP Activity Scores]
    H --> K[Cell-Cell Communication]
```

The model leverages **graph convolutional neural networks** to encode spatial relationships and **masked linear decoders** to ensure interpretability of gene program activity. Key components include the encoder with configurable GCN or GAT layers, gene expression decoder, edge reconstruction decoder, and latent GP embeddings.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L24-L248), [mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb#L200-L250)

## Prerequisites

NicheCompass requires:
- **Python 3.10**
- **GPU support** recommended (Apple silicon and multi-GPU not yet supported)
- **Virtual environment** (conda, python-venv, or Docker)

**Hardware Requirements**:
- Minimum: 8GB RAM, 4GB GPU memory
- Recommended: 16GB+ RAM, 8GB+ GPU memory

> [!TIP]
> For training on multimodal data (RNA + ATAC-seq), we strongly recommend using conda environments due to bedtools dependency.

Sources: [installation.md](docs/installation.md#L1-L20)

## Installation

### Step 1: Create Virtual Environment

```bash
# Using python-venv (fastest for unimodal training)
python3 -m venv nichecompass_env
source nichecompass_env/bin/activate
pip install uv

# OR using conda (recommended for multimodal training)
conda create -n nichecompass_env python=3.10 -c conda-forge
conda activate nichecompass_env
```

Sources: [installation.md](docs/installation.md#L22-L38)

### Step 2: Install External Dependencies

**Option A: Using environment.yaml (Recommended for beginners)**

```bash
conda env create -f environment.yaml
```

This installs PyTorch 2.0.0 with CUDA 11.7, PyTorch Scatter, PyTorch Sparse, and bedtools.

Sources: [environment.yaml](environment.yaml#L1-L15), [installation.md](docs/installation.md#L60-L70)

**Option B: Manual installation (More control)**

```bash
# Install PyTorch with GPU support
uv pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu124

# Install PyTorch Geometric extensions
uv pip install pyg_lib torch_scatter torch_sparse -f https://data.pyg.org/whl/torch-2.6.0+cu124.html

# Install bedtools (required for ATAC-seq data)
conda install bedtools=2.30.0 -c bioconda
```

Sources: [installation.md](docs/installation.md#L40-L60)

### Step 3: Install NicheCompass

```bash
# Core installation
uv pip install nichecompass

# With all optional dependencies (tutorials, benchmarking, etc.)
uv pip install nichecompass[all]
```

Sources: [installation.md](docs/installation.md#L72-L80)

## Quick Start Workflow

The complete NicheCompass pipeline follows this sequence:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[1. Setup<br/>Import libraries & define paths] --> B[2. Prepare Gene Programs<br/>Load from databases]
    B --> C[3. Load Data<br/>Read AnnData & compute spatial graph]
    C --> D[4. Add GP Masks<br/>Integrate into AnnData]
    D --> E[5. Train Model<br/>Initialize & optimize]
    E --> F[6. Analysis<br/>Extract insights]
    
    style A fill:#e3f2fd
    style B fill:#bbdefb
    style C fill:#90caf9
    style D fill:#64b5f6
    style E fill:#42a5f5
    style F fill:#2196f3
```

Sources: [mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb#L50-L650)

## Step-by-Step Tutorial

### 1. Setup and Configuration

```python
import os
import numpy as np
import scanpy as sc
import squidpy as sq
from nichecompass.models import NicheCompass
from nichecompass.utils import (
    extract_gp_dict_from_omnipath_lr_interactions,
    extract_gp_dict_from_nichenet_lrt_interactions,
    extract_gp_dict_from_mebocost_ms_interactions,
    filter_and_combine_gp_dict_gps_v2,
    add_gps_from_gp_dict_to_adata,
    create_new_color_dict
)

# Define paths
ga_data_folder_path = "data/gene_annotations"
gp_data_folder_path = "data/gene_programs"
so_data_folder_path = "data/spatial_omics"
model_folder_path = "artifacts/single_sample/model"
figure_folder_path = "artifacts/single_sample/figures"
```

Sources: [mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb#L50-L120)

### 2. Create Prior Knowledge Gene Programs

NicheCompass uses biological prior knowledge through gene programs (GPs). These represent inter- and intracellular communication pathways that make the latent space interpretable.

**Available GP Sources**:

| Database | Type | Description | Example GPs |
|----------|------|-------------|-------------|
| **OmniPath** | Ligand-Receptor | Curated signaling pathways | EGFR-ERBB2, PDGF-PDGFR |
| **NicheNet** | Combined | Ligand-receptor-target interactions | WNT signaling, Notch pathway |
| **MEBOCOST** | Metabolic | Enzyme-sensor interactions | ATP-AMP, Glucose transport |
| **CollecTRI** | TF Regulation | Transcription factor networks | TP53 targets, MYC targets |

```python
species = "mouse"

# Extract gene programs from databases
omnipath_gp_dict = extract_gp_dict_from_omnipath_lr_interactions(
    species=species,
    lr_network_file_path=f"{gp_data_folder_path}/omnipath_lr_network.csv",
    gene_orthologs_mapping_file_path=f"{ga_data_folder_path}/human_mouse_gene_orthologs.csv"
)

nichenet_gp_dict = extract_gp_dict_from_nichenet_lrt_interactions(
    species=species,
    lr_network_file_path=f"{gp_data_folder_path}/nichenet_lr_network_v2_mouse.csv",
    ligand_target_matrix_file_path=f"{gp_data_folder_path}/nichenet_ligand_target_matrix_v2_mouse.csv",
    max_n_target_genes_per_gp=250
)

mebocost_gp_dict = extract_gp_dict_from_mebocost_ms_interactions(
    species=species,
    dir_path=f"{gp_data_folder_path}/metabolite_enzyme_sensor_gps"
)

# Filter and combine gene programs
gp_dicts = [omnipath_gp_dict, nichenet_gp_dict, mebocost_gp_dict]
combined_gp_dict = filter_and_combine_gp_dict_gps_v2(gp_dicts, verbose=True)

print(f"Total gene programs: {len(combined_gp_dict)}")
```

Sources: [gene_programs.py](src/nichecompass/utils/gene_programs.py#L600-L771), [mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb#L220-L360)

### 3. Load Spatial Data and Compute Neighborhood Graph

```python
# Load AnnData object (pre-processed spatial data)
adata = sc.read_h5ad(f"{so_data_folder_path/starmap_plus_mouse_cns.h5ad")

# Compute spatial neighborhood graph
n_neighbors = 4  # Adjust based on your data's interaction range
sq.gr.spatial_neighbors(
    adata,
    coord_type="generic",
    spatial_key="spatial",
    n_neighs=n_neighbors
)

# Make adjacency matrix symmetric
adata.obsp["spatial_connectivities"] = (
    adata.obsp["spatial_connectivities"].maximum(
        adata.obsp["spatial_connectivities"].T
    )
)

# Add gene program masks to AnnData
add_gps_from_gp_dict_to_adata(
    gp_dict=combined_gp_dict,
    adata=adata,
    gp_targets_mask_key="nichecompass_gp_targets",
    gp_sources_mask_key="nichecompass_gp_sources",
    gp_names_key="nichecompass_gp_names",
    min_genes_per_gp=2
)

print(f"Cells: {adata.n_obs}, Genes: {adata.n_vars}")
```

Sources: [mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb#L400-L480), [gene_programs.py](src/nichecompass/utils/gene_programs.py#L18-L40)

### 4. Initialize and Train Model

**Key Configuration Parameters**:

| Parameter | Recommended Range | Description |
|-----------|------------------|-------------|
| `conv_layer_encoder` | `"gcnconv"` or `"gatv2conv"` | Graph convolution type (GATv2 is more accurate but slower) |
| `n_neighbors` | 4-10 | Spatial neighborhood size |
| `n_epochs` | 300-500 | Training epochs |
| `n_epochs_all_gps` | 20-50 | Initial training with all GPs active |
| `lambda_edge_recon` | 100000-500000 | Edge reconstruction loss weight |
| `lambda_gene_expr_recon` | 200-500 | Gene expression reconstruction weight |
| `lambda_l1_addon` | 20-50 | De novo GP regularization |

```python
# Initialize NicheCompass model
model = NicheCompass(
    adata=adata,
    counts_key="counts",
    adj_key="spatial_connectivities",
    gp_names_key="nichecompass_gp_names",
    active_gp_names_key="nichecompass_active_gp_names",
    gp_targets_mask_key="nichecompass_gp_targets",
    gp_sources_mask_key="nichecompass_gp_sources",
    latent_key="nichecompass_latent",
    conv_layer_encoder="gcnconv",  # Use "gatv2conv" for better accuracy
    active_gp_thresh_ratio=0.01
)

# Train the model
model.train(
    n_epochs=400,
    n_epochs_all_gps=25,
    lr=0.001,
    lambda_edge_recon=500000,
    lambda_gene_expr_recon=300,
    lambda_l1_masked=0,
    lambda_l1_addon=30,
    edge_batch_size=256,
    use_cuda_if_available=True,
    verbose=True
)

# Compute latent space embedding
sc.pp.neighbors(model.adata, use_rep="nichecompass_latent")
sc.tl.umap(model.adata)

# Save model
model.save(dir_path=model_folder_path, overwrite=True, save_adata=True)
```

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L590-L620), [mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb#L530-L580)

### 5. Initial Analysis

```python
# Visualize latent space
cell_type_colors = create_new_color_dict(
    adata=model.adata,
    cat_key="cell_type"
)

# UMAP of latent space
sc.pl.umap(
    model.adata,
    color=["cell_type"],
    palette=cell_type_colors,
    title="Cell Types in NicheCompass Latent Space"
)

# Spatial visualization
sc.pl.spatial(
    model.adata,
    color="cell_type",
    palette=cell_type_colors,
    spot_size=40
)

# Get active gene programs
active_gps = model.get_active_gps()
print(f"Active gene programs: {len(active_gps)}")

# Get latent representation
latent = model.get_latent_representation()
print(f"Latent shape: {latent.shape}")
```

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L1264-L1276), [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L1235-L1250), [mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb#L700-L750)

> [!TIP]
> Always start with the default hyperparameters. The balance between `lambda_edge_recon` and `lambda_gene_expr_recon` is crucial - higher edge weights improve niche identification while higher gene expression weights improve GP recovery.

## Common Use Cases

NicheCompass supports several analytical workflows. Choose based on your research question:

| Use Case | Tutorial | Key Features |
|----------|----------|--------------|
| **Single sample analysis** | `mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb` | Niche identification, GP activity, spatial patterns |
| **Sample integration** | `mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb` | Multi-sample atlas, batch correction, joint embeddings |
| **Reference mapping** | `mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb` | Map new samples to references, query analysis |
| **Multimodal analysis** | `mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb` | RNA + ATAC-seq integration, chromatin accessibility |

Sources: [tutorials/index.md](docs/tutorials/index.md#L1-L12)

# Installation and Setup



NicheCompass is a comprehensive toolkit for end-to-end analysis of spatial multi-omics data, enabling spatial atlas building, niche identification, and characterization through cellular graph embeddings. This guide walks you through the complete installation process, from environment setup to dependency management, with specialized recommendations for different use cases.

![NicheCompass Logo](https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/nichecompass/blob/main/docs/_static/nichecompass_logo_readme.png?raw=true)

## System Requirements

Before proceeding with installation, ensure your system meets the following requirements:

| Requirement | Specification | Notes |
|------------|---------------|-------|
| **Python Version** | 3.10 | Only Python 3.10 is supported [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml#L19) |
| **Operating System** | Linux (POSIX) | Primary support for Linux systems [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml#L24) |
| **GPU Support** | CUDA-compatible GPU | Recommended for training models |
| **GPU Frameworks** | CUDA 11.7+ or 12.4 | Specific versions required for PyTorch compatibility |
| **Memory** | 8GB+ RAM minimum | 16GB+ recommended for multi-modal training |
| **Storage** | 5GB+ free space | For dependencies and model checkpoints |

> [!TIP]
> Apple silicon and multi-GPU training are not yet supported. For optimal performance, use a single NVIDIA GPU with CUDA support.

## Installation Architecture

The installation process follows a modular architecture with multiple pathways depending on your use case:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Start Installation] --> B{Choose Use Case}
    
    B --> C[Multi-modal Training<br/>RNA + ATAC-seq]
    B --> D[Uni-modal Training<br/>RNA only]
    B --> E[Development/Docs<br/>Contributing]
    
    C --> F[Conda Environment<br/>Recommended]
    D --> G[pip + uv<br/>Fastest]
    E --> H[pip + optional groups<br/>Flexible]
    
    F --> I[Install External Libraries<br/>PyTorch, PyG, bedtools]
    G --> I
    H --> I
    
    I --> J[Install NicheCompass Core]
    
    J --> K{Select Optional Features}
    K --> L[Benchmarking<br/>scib-metrics, jax]
    K --> M[Multi-modal<br/>scglue]
    K --> N[Tutorials<br/>jupyterlab]
    K --> O[All Features<br/>Complete suite]
    
    L --> P[Verify Installation]
    M --> P
    N --> P
    O --> P
    
    P --> Q[Ready to Use]
    
    style C fill:#ff9999
    style D fill:#99ff99
    style E fill:#9999ff
    style F fill:#ffcccc
    style G fill:#ccffcc
    style I fill:#ffcc99
```

## Environment Setup

### Virtual Environment Recommendation

We strongly discourage installing NicheCompass directly into your system Python. Instead, create an isolated virtual environment to prevent dependency conflicts and maintain system stability.

#### Option 1: Conda Environment (Recommended for Multi-modal)

Conda provides the most robust environment management for scientific computing workflows, especially when handling complex dependencies like PyTorch and bioinformatics tools.

```bash
# Create conda environment using provided configuration
conda env create -f environment.yaml
```

The provided [environment.yaml](environment.yaml#L1-L15) includes:
- Python 3.10
- PyTorch 2.0.0 with CUDA 11.7
- PyTorch Scatter 2.1.1
- PyTorch Sparse 0.6.17
- bedtools 2.30.0 (for ATAC-seq processing)

Activate your environment:
```bash
conda activate nichecompass
```

#### Option 2: Python venv + uv (Fastest for Uni-modal)

For rapid installation and uni-modal workflows, the `uv` package manager within a Python virtual environment provides significantly faster dependency resolution [docs/installation.md](docs/installation.md#L16-L21):

```bash
# Create and activate virtual environment
python3 -m venv ${/path/to/new/virtual/environment}
source ${/path/to/new/virtual/environment}/bin/activate

# Install uv for fast package management
pip install uv
```

Replace `${/path/to/new/virtual/environment}` with your desired installation path.

## External Library Dependencies

Before installing NicheCompass, you must install several external libraries that are not included in the core package.

### PyTorch Ecosystem

The PyTorch ecosystem forms the foundation for NicheCompass's deep learning capabilities:

| Library | Purpose | Recommended Version |
|---------|---------|-------------------|
| **PyTorch** | Core deep learning framework | 2.0.0+ or 2.6.0+ |
| **PyTorch Scatter** | Efficient scatter operations | 2.1.1+ |
| **PyTorch Sparse** | Sparse tensor operations | 0.6.17+ |

#### Installing PyTorch with CUDA Support

For CUDA-enabled GPU acceleration, install PyTorch using the specific version matching your CUDA setup [docs/installation.md](docs/installation.md#L40-L51):

**For PyTorch 2.6.0 with CUDA 12.4 (Latest Recommended):**
```bash
uv pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu124
uv pip install pyg_lib torch_scatter torch_sparse -f https://data.pyg.org/whl/torch-2.6.0+cu124.html
```

**For PyTorch 2.0.0 with CUDA 11.7 (Stable/Conda):**
```bash
uv pip install torch==2.0.0+cu117 --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu117
uv pip install pyg_lib torch_scatter torch_sparse -f https://data.pyg.org/whl/torch-2.0.0+cu117.html
```

Replace `cu124` or `cu117` with your specific CUDA version if different.

### Bioinformatics Tools

#### bedtools (Multi-modal Only)

Required only for processing paired ATAC-seq data in multi-modal workflows [docs/installation.md](docs/installation.md#L54-L56):

```bash
conda install bedtools=2.30.0 -c bioconda
```

> [!TIP]
> If you're working exclusively with RNA-seq spatial data (uni-modal), you can skip bedtools installation to reduce dependency complexity.

## NicheCompass Installation

### Core Installation

Once external dependencies are installed, proceed with installing the NicheCompass package itself [docs/installation.md](docs/installation.md#L63-L66):

```bash
# Basic installation
uv pip install nichecompass
```

NicheCompass offers several optional dependency groups to extend functionality for specific use cases [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml#L55-L87):

#### Installation Options Comparison

| Option | Command | Use Case | Additional Dependencies |
|--------|---------|----------|------------------------|
| **Basic** | `uv pip install nichecompass` | Core spatial analysis | None |
| **All Features** | `uv pip install nichecompass[all]` | Complete functionality | dev, docs, tests, benchmarking, multimodal, tutorials |
| **Benchmarking** | `uv pip install nichecompass[benchmarking]` | Model evaluation and comparison | scib-metrics, pynndescent, scikit-misc, squidpy, jax, jaxlib |
| **Multi-modal** | `uv pip install nichecompass[multimodal]` | RNA + ATAC-seq integration | scglue |
| **Tutorials** | `uv pip install nichecompass[tutorials]` | Running tutorial notebooks | jupyterlab |

#### Installing All Optional Features

For the most complete installation experience [docs/installation.md](docs/installation.md#L68-L70):

```bash
uv pip install nichecompass[all]
```

This installs:
- **Development tools**: pre-commit, twine
- **Documentation**: Sphinx ecosystem with Sphinx Book Theme
- **Testing**: pytest, coverage
- **Benchmarking**: scib-metrics, jax/jaxlib for GPU acceleration
- **Multi-modal**: scglue for ATAC-seq integration
- **Tutorials**: JupyterLab for interactive learning

### JAX GPU Support (Benchmarking Enhancement)

For accelerated benchmarking capabilities, enable GPU support for JAX after installation [docs/installation.md](docs/installation.md#L72-L78):

```bash
# For CUDA 12
uv pip install jax[cuda12]

# For CUDA 11
uv pip install jax[cuda11]
```

Replace with your major CUDA version (11 or 12).

## Troubleshooting

### Common Installation Issues

| Issue | Likely Cause | Solution |
|-------|--------------|----------|
| **CUDA version mismatch** | PyTorch compiled for different CUDA version | Verify `nvcc --version` matches installed PyTorch CUDA version |
| **Import errors for PyTorch Scatter/Sparse** | Version incompatibility with PyTorch | Install from PyG wheel index matching your PyTorch version |
| **bedtools not found** | Not in PATH after conda install | Ensure bioconda channel is prioritized: `conda config --add channels bioconda` |
| **Out of memory during training** | Insufficient GPU memory | Reduce batch size or use CPU fallback (not recommended) |
| **JAX GPU not working** | Missing CUDA-compatible JAX installation | Reinstall JAX with correct CUDA version specifier |

### Dependency Conflicts

If you encounter dependency conflicts between NicheCompass and other packages in your environment:

1. **Use a fresh environment**: Create a new conda environment or virtual environment
2. **Check version constraints**: Review [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml) for specific version requirements
3. **Install in order**: External libraries first, then NicheCompass
4. **Use conda-forge**: For bioinformatics dependencies, conda-forge often provides better compatibility

# NicheCompass Model Architecture and Core Concepts



This page provides a comprehensive overview of the NicheCompass model architecture, its core components, and the fundamental concepts that power spatial transcriptomics analysis. NicheCompass is a **Variational Gene Program Graph Autoencoder (VGPGAE)** designed to model cellular niches by integrating spatial gene expression, chromatin accessibility, and prior biological knowledge through gene programs.

![NicheCompass Architecture Overview](https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/nichecompass/blob/main/docs/_static/nichecompass_fig1.png?raw=true)

## Architectural Foundations

The NicheCompass model implements a sophisticated **graph-based variational autoencoder** that operates on spatial omics data as nodes in a cellular neighborhood graph. At its core, the model learns to represent each cell as a combination of **gene programs**—biological modules that capture coordinated gene expression patterns—which can then be used for downstream analyses including cell-cell communication inference, differential testing, and multi-sample integration.

The architecture follows a modular design where the **NicheCompass** class serves as the high-level API, inheriting model management capabilities from **BaseModelMixin**, while the **VGPGAE** module implements the actual neural network computations. This separation enables flexible experimentation with network components while maintaining a stable user-facing interface.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L1-L24), [basemodelmixin.py](src/nichecompass/models/basemodelmixin.py#L1-L4), [vgpgae.py](src/nichecompass/modules/vgpgae.py#L1-L4)

## Core Neural Network Architecture

### VGPGAE Module Structure

The **Variational Gene Program Graph Autoencoder** serves as the computational engine of NicheCompass, implementing a sophisticated graph neural network architecture that simultaneously learns gene program representations and reconstructs both node features and graph structure. The module supports both **prior knowledge gene programs** (derived from external databases) and **addon gene programs** (learned de novo during training), enabling a hybrid approach to biological discovery.

The VGPGAE module accepts key architectural parameters including the number of encoder layers, hidden dimensions, number of prior/addon gene programs, and choice of graph convolution layer (GCN or GATv2). The module maintains separate decoders for different reconstruction tasks: a graph decoder for spatial connectivity, a gene expression decoder for RNA-seq data, and optionally a chromatin accessibility decoder for ATAC-seq data.

Sources: [vgpgae.py](src/nichecompass/modules/vgpgae.py#L146-L250), [vgpgae.py](src/nichecompass/modules/vgpgae.py#L32-L35)

### Forward Pass Architecture

The forward pass of VGPGAE demonstrates the model's dual-path architecture designed to handle both edge-level and node-level reconstruction tasks. When processing an edge-level batch, the model focuses on reconstructing spatial relationships between cells. When processing a node-level batch, it concentrates on reconstructing omics features (gene expression and chromatin accessibility).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Input Data Batch] --> B{Decoder Type?}
    B -->|Graph Decoder| C[Edge-level Batch]
    B -->|Omics Decoder| D[Node-level Batch]
    
    C --> E["Sample Positive/Negative Edges"]
    E --> F[Extract Node Features for Edge Endpoints]
    F --> G[Graph Convolution Processing]
    G --> H[Edge Reconstruction]
    
    D --> I[Sample Nodes]
    I --> J[Extract Node Features]
    J --> K[Graph Convolution Processing]
    K --> L[Latent Space Sampling]
    L --> M[Omics Features Reconstruction]
    
    G --> N[Common Components]
    K --> N
    N --> O[Optional Categorical Covariates Injection]
    O --> P[Gene Program Representation]
```

The model applies **logarithmic transformation** to omics features for encoder input when `log_variational=True`, improving numerical stability. The graph convolution layers process both node features and spatial connectivity information, while categorical covariate embeddings can be injected at multiple points (encoder, gene expression decoder, chromatin accessibility decoder) to incorporate metadata into the representation learning process.

Sources: [vgpgae.py](src/nichecompass/modules/vgpgae.py#L541-L600), [encoders.py](src/nichecompass/nn/encoders.py#L144-L170)

## Encoder Design

### Graph Convolution Encoder

The **Encoder** component implements a variational graph neural network that maps high-dimensional omics features to a low-dimensional latent space representing gene program activities. The encoder supports two graph convolution strategies: **GCN (Graph Convolutional Network)** and **GATv2 (Graph Attention Network version 2)**, with GATv2 being the default choice for its ability to learn attention weights between neighboring cells.

The encoder architecture begins with optional injection of categorical covariate embeddings into the input features, followed by fully-connected layers and graph convolution layers. For GATv2, multiple attention heads can be specified, allowing the model to learn different types of relationships between neighboring cells. The encoder outputs both **mean (mu)** and **log standard deviation (logstd)** parameters for each gene program, defining a Gaussian distribution from which latent representations are sampled during training.

Sources: [encoders.py](src/nichecompass/nn/encoders.py#L55-L68), [encoders.py](src/nichecompass/nn/encoders.py#L144-L180)

> [!TIP]
> The encoder's variational formulation encourages the learned latent space to be smooth and continuous, which enables biological interpolation between cell states and improves generalization to new spatial datasets.

### Categorical Covariate Integration

Categorical covariates such as batch identifiers, tissue regions, or experimental conditions are integrated through learned embeddings that can be injected at multiple points in the network. These embeddings capture discrete metadata information that might otherwise be confounded with biological signals, allowing the model to explicitly model technical and batch effects rather than having them leak into gene program representations.

The injection is controlled by the `cat_covariates_embeds_injection` parameter, which accepts a list specifying which components receive the embeddings: the encoder, the gene expression decoder, the chromatin accessibility decoder, or any combination thereof. This flexibility enables different modeling strategies depending on the analysis goals.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L205-L210), [encoders.py](src/nichecompass/nn/encoders.py#L144-L150)

## Decoder Architectures

### Graph Decoder for Spatial Connectivity

The **CosineSimGraphDecoder** implements a lightweight decoder that reconstructs spatial edges based on cosine similarity between latent representations of connected cells. This approach encourages the model to learn representations where cells that are spatially close have similar gene program activities, effectively preserving neighborhood structure in the latent space.

The decoder operates by computing the dot product of normalized latent vectors, producing logits that represent the probability of edge existence. During training, the model learns to distinguish true spatial connections (positive edges) from randomly sampled non-connections (negative edges) through binary cross-entropy loss.

Sources: [decoders.py](src/nichecompass/nn/decoders.py#L14-L41), [losses.py](src/nichecompass/modules/losses.py#L123-L167)

### Omics Feature Decoders

#### MaskedOmicsFeatureDecoder

The **MaskedOmicsFeatureDecoder** is the primary decoder for reconstructing omics features from latent gene program representations. It implements a **masked linear architecture** where each gene program has learnable weights only for a predefined subset of genes or chromatin peaks, enforced through binary masks derived from prior biological knowledge.

The decoder applies gene program-specific weights to the latent representation and combines them linearly to reconstruct normalized feature means, which are then scaled by the library size to account for varying sequencing depth. For ATAC-seq data, the decoder supports **dynamic masking** where peaks corresponding to genes that have been regularized out (weight set to zero) are also disabled, ensuring consistency between modalities.

Sources: [decoders.py](src/nichecompass/nn/decoders.py#L65-L138), [decoders.py](src/nichecompass/nn/decoders.py#L133-L170)

#### FCOmicsFeatureDecoder

An alternative **FCOmicsFeatureDecoder** uses a fully-connected architecture without gene program-specific masking, providing more flexibility but reduced biological interpretability. This decoder can be enabled through the `use_fc_decoder` parameter and is typically used for ablation studies or when prior gene program masks are not available.

Sources: [decoders.py](src/nichecompass/nn/decoders.py#L172-L239)

## Loss Functions and Optimization Objectives

NicheCompass employs a **multi-objective loss function** that balances several competing objectives to learn biologically meaningful gene programs while maintaining reconstruction accuracy and spatial structure preservation.

| Loss Component | Purpose | Default Lambda |
|---------------|---------|----------------|
| Gene Expression Reconstruction | Reconstruct RNA-seq counts using negative binomial distribution | 300.0 |
| Chromatin Accessibility Reconstruction | Reconstruct ATAC-seq counts using negative binomial distribution | 100.0 |
| Edge Reconstruction | Preserve spatial connectivity through cosine similarity decoder | 500,000.0 |
| KL Divergence | Encourage smooth, complete latent space representation | Implicit in variational formulation |
| L1 Regularization (Masked) | Enforce sparsity in prior gene program gene weights | User-specified |
| L1 Regularization (Addon) | Enforce sparsity in addon gene program gene weights | 30.0 |
| Group Lasso | Enforce sparsity across gene programs (entire programs can be disabled) | User-specified |
| Categorical Covariates Contrastive | Separate cells by categorical covariates in latent space | User-specified |

Sources: [vgpgae.py](src/nichecompass/modules/vgpgae.py#L932-L1000), [losses.py](src/nichecompass/modules/losses.py#L255-L292)

### KL Divergence Regularization

The **KL divergence loss** encourages encoder outputs to follow a standard normal distribution, preventing overfitting and ensuring the latent space is well-structured for downstream analyses. This is computed using the standard variational autoencoder formulation from Kingma & Welling (2013), summing over gene programs and averaging over nodes in each batch.

Sources: [losses.py](src/nichecompass/modules/losses.py#L255-L292)

### Negative Binomial Reconstruction Loss

Both RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data are modeled using the **negative binomial distribution**, which accounts for over-dispersion common in count data. The reconstruction loss computes the negative log-likelihood under the predicted distribution parameters (mean and dispersion theta), encouraging the model to learn accurate reconstructions of the raw count data.

Sources: [losses.py](src/nichecompass/modules/losses.py#L169-L213)

## Gene Program Concepts

### Prior vs Addon Gene Programs

NicheCompass supports two types of gene programs:

**Prior Gene Programs**: Derived from external databases such as pathway databases (KEGG, Reactome), gene sets from MSigDB, or domain-specific collections. These are provided as input through binary masks indicating which genes belong to which program. Prior gene programs provide biological interpretability by grounding learned representations in known biology.

**Addon Gene Programs**: Learned de novo during training without prior constraints. These capture novel patterns not represented in the prior knowledge, such as cell-type-specific programs, tissue-specific responses, or technical artifacts. The number of addon gene programs is controlled by the `n_addon_gp` parameter (default: 100).

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L191-L204), [vgpgae.py](src/nichecompass/modules/vgpgae.py#L146-L156)

### Active Gene Programs

Not all gene programs are equally relevant for a given dataset. NicheCompass identifies **active gene programs** through a thresholding mechanism based on the aggregated absolute weights of genes in each program. Programs with total weights below a threshold (`active_gp_thresh_ratio`, default: 0.01 for NicheCompass, 0.03 for VGPGAE) relative to the strongest program are considered inactive and excluded from downstream analyses.

The active program determination supports multiple aggregation modes:
- **sum**: Prioritizes programs reconstructing many genes
- **nzmeans**: Normalizes by number of genes, prioritizing strong, focused programs
- **sum+nzmeans**: Combines both approaches (default)

Sources: [vgpgae.py](src/nichecompass/modules/vgpgae.py#L1204-L1260), [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L231-L234)

### Target vs Source Genes

Gene programs can have different roles in cell-cell communication:

**Target Genes**: Genes that are affected or regulated by the gene program, typically representing downstream effects or responsive genes.

**Source Genes**: Genes that drive or activate the gene program, potentially representing ligands, receptors, or upstream regulators that mediate intercellular signaling.

This distinction is crucial for cell-cell communication analysis, where source programs in one cell type can affect target programs in neighboring cell types. The masks are stored separately and can be used for different regularization strategies.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L195-L201), [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L202-L204)

## Multi-modal Data Integration

### RNA and ATAC-seq Joint Modeling

NicheCompass supports **multi-modal analysis** through joint modeling of gene expression (RNA-seq) and chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) data from the same spatial locations. The architecture includes parallel decoders for each modality, with the option to link them through **gene-peak masks** that indicate which chromatin peaks are associated with which genes.

The joint modeling enables cross-modal imputation (predicting ATAC from RNA or vice versa), integration of regulatory information (linking accessibility to expression), and more comprehensive characterization of cellular states. The model can be configured to include or exclude each modality's reconstruction loss independently.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L191-L192), [vgpgae.py](src/nichecompass/modules/vgpgae.py#L158-L163)

### Dynamic Cross-modal Masking

A sophisticated feature of multi-modal integration is **dynamic masking**, where the ATAC decoder's mask is updated based on RNA decoder activity. If a gene is regularized out of a gene program (its weight set to zero), the associated chromatin peaks are also disabled from that program. This ensures consistency between modalities and prevents the model from using accessibility signals for genes that are not considered active in the RNA representation.

Sources: [vgpgae.py](src/nichecompass/modules/vgpgae.py#L541-L547), [decoders.py](src/nichecompass/nn/decoders.py#L133-L145)

## Model Training Strategy

### Staged Training Protocol

NicheCompass implements a **staged training approach** that gradually introduces different loss components:

1. **Initial Phase (first 25 epochs)**: Train with all gene programs enabled to establish robust initial representations
2. **Edge Reconstruction Phase**: If `n_epochs_no_edge_recon` is specified, begin without edge reconstruction loss, then introduce it later
3. **Categorical Contrastive Phase**: If `n_epochs_no_cat_covariates_contrastive` is specified, introduce contrastive loss after initial epochs
4. **Fine-tuning Phase**: Continue training with all active components, potentially with different learning rates or regularization strengths

This staged approach helps stabilize training and prevents the model from converging to poor local optima due to competing objectives early in training.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L590-L620)

### Batch Sampling Strategy

Training uses sophisticated batch sampling strategies for both edge and node batches:

- **Edge Batches**: Sample a mix of positive (existing spatial edges) and negative (non-edges) connections, with the number controlled by `edge_batch_size` parameter (default: 256)
- **Node Batches**: Sample individual cells along with their neighbors for message passing, with size controlled by `node_batch_size` parameter

This efficient sampling enables training on large spatial datasets while maintaining the computational benefits of mini-batch stochastic gradient descent.

Sources: [vgpgae.py](src/nichecompass/modules/vgpgae.py#L541-L580), [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L610-L612)

## Key Configuration Parameters

The following table summarizes the most important architectural parameters and their typical values:

| Parameter | Category | Description | Default |
|-----------|----------|-------------|---------|
| `conv_layer_encoder` | Architecture | Graph convolution type: "gcnconv" or "gatv2conv" | "gatv2conv" |
| `n_layers_encoder` | Architecture | Number of graph convolution layers | 1 |
| `n_hidden_encoder` | Architecture | Hidden dimension size | Auto-calculated |
| `encoder_n_attention_heads` | Architecture | Number of attention heads for GATv2 | 4 |
| `n_addon_gp` | Gene Programs | Number of de novo gene programs to learn | 100 |
| `active_gp_thresh_ratio` | Gene Programs | Threshold for determining active programs | 0.01 |
| `active_gp_type` | Gene Programs | Whether to evaluate prior/addon programs separately | "separate" |
| `lambda_gene_expr_recon` | Loss Weight | Weight for RNA reconstruction loss | 300.0 |
| `lambda_chrom_access_recon` | Loss Weight | Weight for ATAC reconstruction loss | 100.0 |
| `lambda_edge_recon` | Loss Weight | Weight for edge reconstruction loss | 500,000.0 |
| `lambda_l1_addon` | Loss Weight | L1 regularization for addon programs | 30.0 |
| `node_label_method` | Graph Processing | Method for aggregating neighbor information | "one-hop-norm" |

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L234-L248), [vgpgae.py](src/nichecompass/modules/vgpgae.py#L165-L190)

> [!TIP]
> The default loss weights reflect the different scales of each component: edge reconstruction receives the highest weight because it operates on binary values, while omics reconstruction receives lower weights because count data has larger magnitude and is modeled through probabilistic likelihoods.

## Latent Space Representation

The latent space learned by NicheCompass represents each cell as a vector of **gene program activities**, where each dimension corresponds to the strength of a specific biological program in that cell. This representation has several desirable properties:

- **Interpretability**: Each dimension maps to a known or learned biological program
- **Smoothness**: The variational formulation encourages local continuity
- **Spatial Preservation**: Edge reconstruction maintains neighborhood relationships
- **Multi-modal Integration**: Captures signals from both RNA and ATAC when available

The latent representation can be extracted for visualization, clustering, trajectory inference, or as input to downstream machine learning models. The `get_latent_representation` method provides flexible options for whether to return only the mean or both mean and variance, and whether to include only active programs.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L1264-L1276), [vgpgae.py](src/nichecompass/modules/vgpgae.py#L1368-L1374)

## Model Inference and Analysis

Once trained, the NicheCompass model provides a comprehensive API for extracting insights:

- **Gene Program Data**: Retrieve gene program names, weights, and activities through `get_gp_data` and `get_gp_weights`
- **Differential Testing**: Perform statistical tests to identify gene programs that differ between conditions using `run_differential_gp_tests`
- **Importance Scores**: Compute gene or peak importance for specific programs using `compute_gp_gene_importances` or `compute_gp_peak_importances`
- **Edge Reconstruction**: Obtain reconstructed spatial connectivity probabilities using `get_recon_edge_probs`
- **Neighbor Importance**: Analyze which neighbors contribute most to a cell's representation using `get_neighbor_importances`

These analysis capabilities are integrated directly into the model class, providing a seamless workflow from training to biological interpretation.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L1166-L1170), [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L1473-L1480)

# Variational Gene Program Graph Autoencoder (VGPGAE)



The Variational Gene Program Graph Autoencoder (VGPGAE) is the core neural network architecture powering the NicheCompass framework. This sophisticated variational graph autoencoder learns interpretable gene programs that simultaneously reconstruct multi-omics features and preserve spatial relationships between cells in tissue microenvironments. The architecture combines variational inference with graph neural networks to enable biologically meaningful representations that capture both molecular expression patterns and spatial colocalization.

## Architecture Overview

VGPGAE follows a variational autoencoder design pattern adapted for graph-structured spatial omics data. The architecture consists of three primary components: an encoder that maps cell omics profiles to a latent gene program space, a variational reparameterization mechanism, and dual decoder branches for reconstructing both spatial connectivity and omics features.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Input["Input Layer"]
        X[Cell Omics Features x]
        Edge[Spatial Edge Index]
        Cat[Categorical Covariates]
    end
    
    subgraph Encoder["Encoder Network"]
        FC[Fully Connected Layers]
        GCN[Graph Convolutional Layers<br/>GCN/GATv2]
        Mu[μ: Mean Parameters]
        LogStd[logσ: Log Std Dev]
    end
    
    subgraph Variational["Variational Reparameterization"]
        Z[Latent Gene Programs z<br/>Prior GP + Add-on GP]
    end
    
    subgraph Decoders["Dual Decoder Branches"]
        GraphDec[Graph Decoder<br/>Cosine Similarity]
        OmicsDec[Omics Feature Decoders<br/>RNA & ATAC]
    end
    
    subgraph Output["Reconstruction"]
        EdgeRecon[Reconstructed Edge Logits]
        RNARecon[RNA Expression<br/>Negative Binomial]
        ATACRecon[Chromatin Accessibility<br/>Negative Binomial]
    end
    
    X --> FC
    Cat --> FC
    FC --> GCN
    Edge --> GCN
    GCN --> Mu
    GCN --> LogStd
    Mu --> Variational
    LogStd --> Variational
    Variational --> Z
    Z --> GraphDec
    Z --> OmicsDec
    GraphDec --> EdgeRecon
    OmicsDec --> RNARecon
    OmicsDec --> ATACRecon
    
    style Z fill:#e1f5ff
    style GraphDec fill:#fff4e1
    style OmicsDec fill:#ffe1f5
```

The encoder processes spatial omics data through fully connected layers followed by graph convolutional message passing, outputting parameters (μ, logσ) of a latent normal distribution. The reparameterization trick samples latent gene program representations from this distribution during training, while using the mean during inference. Two decoder branches operate in parallel: the graph decoder reconstructs spatial edges using cosine similarity in the latent space, while the omics decoders reconstruct cell expression profiles using masked linear layers constrained by gene program masks.

Sources: [vgpgae.py](src/nichecompass/modules/vgpgae.py#L32-L191), [vgaemodulemixin.py](src/nichecompass/modules/vgaemodulemixin.py#L14-L42), [encoders.py](src/nichecompass/nn/encoders.py#L12-L68)

## Gene Program Latent Space

The latent space of VGPGAE is structured into two distinct types of gene programs, each serving a unique biological purpose:

### Prior Gene Programs
These represent biological knowledge encoded as gene-gene connectivity patterns derived from prior sources like KEGG pathways, Reactome, or gene ontology terms. Prior gene programs provide the model with structured biological constraints and interpretability from the outset.

### Add-on Gene Programs
These are de-novo gene programs learned during training without any prior biological constraints. Add-on gene programs enable the model to discover novel biological processes and technical artifacts that may not be captured in existing databases.

| **Component** | **Dimensionality** | **Source** | **Trainable** | **Biological Interpretation** |
|--------------|-------------------|------------|---------------|------------------------------|
| Prior GP | `n_prior_gp` | External databases | Yes (through decoder weights) | Known biological pathways |
| Add-on GP | `n_addon_gp` | Learned from data | Yes | Novel processes/artifacts |
| Total Latent Space | `n_prior_gp + n_addon_gp` | Combined | Yes | Comprehensive cell states |

The separation into prior and add-on gene programs provides a structured latent space where biological knowledge guides learning while still allowing discovery of novel patterns. During training, L1 and group lasso regularization promote sparsity, ensuring that each gene program activates only for a subset of genes and that only a subset of gene programs remain active.

Sources: [vgpgae.py](src/nichecompass/modules/vgpgae.py#L146-L290), [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L234-L243)

## Encoder Design

The encoder transforms high-dimensional omics feature vectors into low-dimensional latent gene program representations through a multi-stage architecture that integrates both node features and graph structure.

### Architecture Stages

The encoder implements a two-stage processing pipeline:

**Stage 1: Fully Connected Transformation**
Initial fully connected layers reduce dimensionality and extract relevant features from the raw omics data. The number of fully connected layers is configurable (`n_fc_layers_encoder`), with each layer applying a linear transformation followed by ReLU activation and optional batch normalization.

**Stage 2: Graph Convolutional Message Passing**
Graph convolutional layers aggregate information from neighboring cells using either GCNConv (Graph Convolutional Network) or GATv2Conv (Graph Attention Network v2). This step captures spatial context by incorporating features from nearby cells in the tissue. The number of message passing layers (`n_layers_encoder`) determines the receptive field radius for each cell.

### Categorical Covariate Integration

The encoder supports injection of categorical covariates (e.g., sample identity, batch, cell type annotations) as learned embeddings. These embeddings can be concatenated either at the input level or hidden level of the encoder, enabling the model to adjust latent representations based on known covariates.

| **Parameter** | **Type** | **Default** | **Impact** |
|--------------|----------|-------------|------------|
| `n_fc_layers_encoder` | int | 1 | Depth of initial FC transformation |
| `n_layers_encoder` | int | 1 | Receptive field radius for spatial aggregation |
| `n_hidden_encoder` | int | Configured | Dimensionality of hidden representations |
| `conv_layer_encoder` | str | "gcnconv" | Message passing strategy (gcnconv/gatv2conv) |
| `encoder_n_attention_heads` | int | 4 | Number of attention heads for GATv2Conv |
| `encoder_use_bn` | bool | False | Whether to apply batch normalization to μ |
| `dropout_rate_encoder` | float | 0.0 | Dropout probability for regularization |

The encoder outputs two parallel vectors for each cell: μ (mean) and logσ (log standard deviation), which parameterize the latent gene program distribution. These outputs are then used in the variational reparameterization step.

Sources: [encoders.py](src/nichecompass/nn/encoders.py#L12-L128), [vgpgae.py](src/nichecompass/modules/vgpgae.py#L292-L309)

## Variational Reparameterization

VGPGAE employs the reparameterization trick to enable gradient-based optimization of the variational lower bound. This technique allows the model to sample from the latent distribution while maintaining differentiability for backpropagation.

### Reparameterization Implementation

The VGAEModuleMixin provides the reparameterization logic:

During training, latent gene program scores are sampled as:
```
z = μ + σ ⊙ ε
```
where ε ~ N(0, I) is random noise sampled from a standard normal distribution and ⊙ denotes element-wise multiplication. This formulation decouples the randomness from the learnable parameters, enabling gradients to flow through μ and σ.

During inference, the model deterministically uses the mean (z = μ), removing stochasticity while preserving the learned latent representation.

This design ensures that:
1. The latent space captures uncertainty in gene program activation
2. Training is stable with low variance gradient estimates
3. Inference is fast and deterministic
4. The model naturally regularizes toward the prior distribution through KL divergence

Sources: [vgaemodulemixin.py](src/nichecompass/modules/vgaemodulemixin.py#L14-L42), [vgpgae.py](src/nichecompass/modules/vgpgae.py#L620-L637)

## Dual Decoder Architecture

VGPGAE employs a dual decoder system where each decoder branch serves a distinct reconstruction purpose, enabling the model to learn representations that preserve both spatial relationships and molecular expression patterns.

### Graph Decoder

The graph decoder reconstructs spatial connectivity between cells using cosine similarity in the latent gene program space. This implementation is motivated by the biological observation that cells with similar gene program activities are likely to be spatially co-located.

**Architecture Details:**
- Computes element-wise cosine similarity between latent representations of node pairs
- Operates on both positive edges (actual spatial connections) and negative edges (sampled non-connections)
- Applies dropout regularization during training
- Outputs edge reconstruction logits (sigmoid activation is integrated into the loss)

The graph decoder enables VGPGAE to learn gene programs that preserve spatial tissue architecture, which is crucial for understanding cellular neighborhoods and microenvironmental interactions.

### Omics Feature Decoders

The omics feature decoders reconstruct molecular profiles using masked linear layers constrained by gene program masks. This design enforces biological interpretability by ensuring that each omics feature can only be reconstructed by a specific subset of gene programs.

**Decoder Types:**
1. **Target Decoder**: Reconstructs the cell's own features (autocrine)
2. **Source Decoder**: Reconstructs aggregated neighborhood features (paracrine)

For each modality (RNA, ATAC), both target and source decoders exist, capturing both cell-intrinsic and microenvironmental influences on expression.

**Negative Binomial Distribution:**
Omics features are modeled using Negative Binomial distributions, which naturally account for:
- Over-dispersion in count data (variance > mean)
- Library size differences between cells
- Dropout events in single-cell technologies

The decoders output two parameters for each feature:
- **μ (mean)**: Scaled by library size and learned from gene program activation
- **θ (dispersion)**: Learned per-feature parameter controlling variance

> [!TIP]
> The separation of target and source decoders enables VGPGAE to distinguish between cell-autonomous gene expression and expression influenced by the microenvironment, which is critical for understanding cell-cell communication in spatial transcriptomics data.

Sources: [decoders.py](src/nichecompass/nn/decoders.py#L14-L169), [vgpgae.py](src/nichecompass/modules/vgpgae.py#L311-L540)

## Forward Pass Execution

The forward pass of VGPGAE operates in two distinct modes depending on the decoder being used, enabling efficient training with different batching strategies.

### Graph Decoder Mode

When operating in graph mode, the forward pass processes edge-level batches for spatial edge reconstruction:

1. **Batch Construction**: Sample positive edges (actual connections) and negative edges (non-connections)
2. **Encoder Forward**: Compute μ and logσ for all nodes in the subgraph
3. **Filter Batch**: Extract representations for source and target nodes of sampled edges
4. **Reparameterization**: Sample latent gene program scores z
5. **Graph Decoder**: Compute cosine similarity between node pair representations
6. **Output**: Edge reconstruction logits

Edge batching is computationally efficient because it only requires processing nodes incident to sampled edges rather than the full graph.

### Omics Decoder Mode

When operating in omics mode, the forward pass processes node-level batches for omics feature reconstruction:

1. **Batch Construction**: Sample individual cells (nodes)
2. **Encoder Forward**: Compute μ and logσ for all nodes in the subgraph
3. **Filter Batch**: Extract representations for sampled nodes
4. **Reparameterization**: Sample latent gene program scores z
5. **Node Label Aggregation**: Aggregate neighborhood features using one-hop methods:
   - **one-hop-norm**: Normalize by neighbor count
   - **one-hop-sum**: Simple sum of neighbor features
   - **one-hop-attention**: Attention-weighted aggregation
6. **Omics Decoders**: Reconstruct target and source omics features
7. **Dynamic Masking**: Apply active GP masks to turn off irrelevant connections
8. **Output**: Distribution parameters for RNA and optionally ATAC

Node batching enables reconstruction of gene expression for individual cells, with source decoders using aggregated neighbor information to capture microenvironmental influence.

> [!TIP]
> The dual-mode forward pass allows VGPGAE to efficiently optimize both edge reconstruction and omics reconstruction simultaneously during training, with different batch sizes and sampling strategies optimized for each objective.

Sources: [vgpgae.py](src/nichecompass/modules/vgpgae.py#L541-L930)

## Loss Computation and Optimization

VGPGAE optimizes a composite objective function combining multiple loss components, each serving a specific regularization or reconstruction purpose.

### Loss Components

**1. Edge Reconstruction Loss**
Binary cross entropy loss between true edge labels and reconstructed edge probabilities. High weighting ensures preservation of spatial architecture.

**2. Gene Expression Reconstruction Loss**
Negative binomial negative log-likelihood loss for RNA expression reconstruction. Computed separately for target (cell-intrinsic) and source (microenvironmental) features.

**3. Chromatin Accessibility Reconstruction Loss**
Negative binomial loss for ATAC-seq peak reconstruction when multi-modal data is available.

**4. KL Divergence Regularization**
Regularization term pushing the variational posterior toward the standard normal prior, preventing overfitting and ensuring well-structured latent space.

**5. L1 Regularization**
- **Masked GP L1**: Applied to genes in prior gene programs to promote sparsity
- **Add-on GP L1**: Applied to genes in add-on gene programs to discover focused programs

**6. Group Lasso Regularization**
Encourages entire gene programs to become inactive if their contribution is negligible, improving interpretability.

**7. Categorical Covariates Contrastive Loss**
Contrastive loss ensuring cells with different categorical covariates (e.g., sample, batch) have distinct latent representations, reducing batch effects.

| **Loss Component** | **Purpose** | **Lambda Parameter** | **Default Value** |
|-------------------|-------------|---------------------|-------------------|
| Edge Reconstruction | Preserve spatial structure | `lambda_edge_recon` | 500000 |
| Gene Expression Recon | Reconstruct RNA expression | `lambda_gene_expr_recon` | 300 |
| Chromatin Access Recon | Reconstruct ATAC peaks | `lambda_chrom_access_recon` | 100 |
| Masked GP L1 | Sparse gene programs | `lambda_l1_masked` | 0 |
| Add-on GP L1 | Sparse add-on programs | `lambda_l1_addon` | 30 |
| Group Lasso | Remove inactive programs | `lambda_group_lasso` | 0 |
| Contrastive | Separate categorical covariates | `lambda_cat_covariates_contrastive` | 0 |

The loss function is computed separately for edge and node batches, with components selectively included in backpropagation based on training phase. This enables curriculum learning strategies where certain losses are activated only after pretraining.

Sources: [vgpgae.py](src/nichecompass/modules/vgpgae.py#L932-L1143), [losses.py](src/nichecompass/modules/losses.py)

## Active Gene Program Detection

VGPGAE dynamically identifies which gene programs are active during training, enabling the model to focus computational resources on biologically relevant programs and improve interpretability.

### Activation Detection Mechanism

The model tracks the mean absolute gene program scores across all cells using an exponential moving average (momentum = 0.1). Active gene programs are identified based on their aggregated importance relative to the most active program:

```
active_threshold = active_gp_thresh_ratio × max(gp_importance)
active_gps = gp_importance > active_threshold
```

The importance of each gene program is computed using multiple aggregation strategies:
- **sum**: Sum of absolute gene weights (prioritizes programs affecting many genes)
- **nzmeans**: Mean of non-zero absolute weights (normalizes by number of genes)
- **sum+nzmeans**: Combination balancing both approaches

### Dynamic Masking

Once gene programs are classified as active or inactive, dynamic masks are applied to disable contributions from inactive programs:

1. **Graph Decoder**: Inactive program scores are set to zero before computing edge similarity
2. **Omics Decoders**: Inactive program-to-gene connections are masked out
3. **Cross-modal Consistency**: For ATAC-seq, peaks are turned off if all connected genes are deactivated in RNA

This dynamic masking ensures that:
- Inactive programs do not influence reconstruction
- Computation is efficient (no processing of inactive pathways)
- Interpretation focuses on biologically relevant programs
- Training is stable (reduced noise from irrelevant dimensions)

The active gene program set evolves during training, with programs potentially becoming active or inactive as the model discovers the most relevant biological processes for the dataset.

Sources: [vgpgae.py](src/nichecompass/modules/vgpgae.py#L640-L660), [vgpgae.py](src/nichecompass/modules/vgpgae.py#L1204-L1335)

## Configuration and Customization

VGPGAE offers extensive configuration options allowing customization for different spatial omics datasets and analysis objectives.

### Key Configuration Categories

**Encoder Architecture:**
- Number of fully connected layers (`n_fc_layers_encoder`)
- Number of graph convolutional layers (`n_layers_encoder`)
- Hidden dimensionality (`n_hidden_encoder`)
- Convolution type (`conv_layer_encoder`: "gcnconv" or "gatv2conv")

**Latent Space Design:**
- Number of prior gene programs (`n_prior_gp`)
- Number of add-on gene programs (`n_addon_gp`)
- Active gene program threshold (`active_gp_thresh_ratio`)

**Loss Weighting:**
- Reconstruction loss weights (edge, gene expression, chromatin accessibility)
- Regularization strengths (L1, group lasso, KL divergence)
- Contrastive loss parameters

**Multi-modal Settings:**
- Whether to include ATAC-seq data
- Gene-peak mapping constraints
- Separate decoder masks for each modality

### Training Strategy Parameters

The training process supports curriculum learning through staged loss activation:

```python
# Early training: Focus on omics reconstruction with edge reconstruction disabled
n_epochs_no_edge_recon = 0  # Set > 0 to disable edge reconstruction initially

# Pretraining: Train all gene programs before applying sparsity
n_epochs_all_gps = 25  # Initial epochs without active GP masking

# Contrastive learning: Delay batch correction until model has learned features
n_epochs_no_cat_covariates_contrastive = 5
```

These strategies enable the model to first learn basic gene program structure before refining with sparsity constraints and spatial reconstruction requirements.

Sources: [vgpgae.py](src/nichecompass/modules/vgpgae.py#L146-L290), [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L590-L628)

## Model Initialization and Integration

VGPGAE is integrated into the broader NicheCompass framework, which handles data processing, model training, and downstream analysis workflows.

### Initialization Pipeline

The NicheCompass model class manages VGPGAE initialization:

1. **Data Validation**: Checks AnnData objects for required attributes (gene program masks, spatial connectivities)
2. **Feature Indexing**: Constructs dictionaries mapping features to gene program associations
3. **Module Instantiation**: Creates VGPGAE module with configured hyperparameters
4. **Device Management**: Handles GPU/CPU placement and data transfer
5. **MLflow Integration**: Logs hyperparameters and metrics for experiment tracking

### Model Access Methods

NicheCompass provides convenient access methods to VGPGAE components:

- `get_latent_representation()`: Extract learned gene program scores
- `get_omics_decoder_outputs()`: Access reconstructed expression distributions
- `get_recon_edge_probs()`: Retrieve reconstructed spatial graph
- `get_active_gps()`: Get list of active gene program names
- `compute_gp_gene_importances()`: Analyze gene contributions to programs
- `get_neighbor_importances()`: Examine cell-cell communication weights

These methods enable downstream analysis including visualization, differential testing, and biological interpretation without needing to directly interact with PyTorch internals.


# Encoder Design and Graph Convolution Strategies



The encoder architecture in NicheCompass implements a sophisticated graph neural network approach for transforming spatial omics data into latent gene program representations. This documentation explores the dual-stage encoder design, graph convolution strategies, and integration mechanisms that enable the model to capture both local cellular contexts and global biological patterns through learned gene program activities.

## Architectural Foundation

The encoder operates as the first critical component in the Variational Gene Program Graph Autoencoder (VGPGAE), transforming high-dimensional omics feature spaces into compact latent representations that encode biological gene program activities. The design follows a hybrid architecture combining fully-connected preprocessing layers with graph-based message passing, allowing the model to learn both feature-level transformations and neighborhood-aware representations.

The encoder receives three primary inputs: omics feature vectors representing gene expression or chromatin accessibility measurements, edge indices defining spatial connectivity between cells/spots, and optional categorical covariates embeddings for batch correction or metadata integration. Through a carefully designed transformation pipeline, these inputs are mapped to a latent space characterized by two complementary components: prior gene programs derived from biological knowledge, and addon gene programs learned de novo from the data.

## Dual-Stage Encoder Architecture

The encoder implements a sequential processing pipeline where fully-connected layers perform initial feature transformation followed by graph convolution layers that incorporate spatial context. This two-stage design allows the model to first learn nonlinear transformations of individual node features, then leverage neighborhood information to refine these representations based on cellular microenvironments.

The fully-connected preprocessing stage supports either single or dual-layer configurations. In the two-layer setup, the first layer reduces input dimensionality by half, followed by a second layer that maps to the hidden dimension size with batch normalization applied. This architecture enables gradual dimensionality reduction while preserving information through intermediate representations. The single-layer configuration provides a direct mapping from input to hidden space for simpler scenarios or when computational efficiency is prioritized.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Input Features<br/>n_input] --> B{Covariate Mode}
    B -->|input| C[Concatenate<br/>Covariate Embedding]
    B -->|hidden| D[FC Layer 1<br/>n_input → n_hidden]
    C --> D
    D --> E{FC Layers}
    E -->|2 layers| F[FC Layer 2<br/>n_input/2 → n_hidden]
    E -->|1 layer| G[Activation & Dropout]
    F --> H[BatchNorm]
    H --> G
    G --> I{Covariate Mode}
    I -->|hidden| J[Concatenate<br/>Covariate Embedding]
    I -->|input| K[Graph Conv Layers]
    J --> K
    K --> L{Conv Layers}
    L -->|2 layers| M[Conv Layer 1<br/>n_hidden → n_hidden]
    L -->|1 layer| N[Final Conv Layers]
    M --> N
    N --> O[Prior GP μ & logσ<br/>n_hidden → n_latent]
    N --> P[Addon GP μ & logσ<br/>n_hidden → n_addon_latent]
    O --> Q[Concatenate<br/>z = [μ_prior, μ_addon]]
    P --> Q
    Q --> R[Latent Representation]
```

The graph convolution stage operates on the transformed feature space from the fully-connected layers, applying message passing along the spatial connectivity graph. Similar to the fully-connected stage, it supports one or two convolutional layers.
