# Latent Representation Extraction and Visualization



Latent representation extraction and visualization form the cornerstone of interpreting NicheCompass model outputs. The model learns gene program activity scores as latent representations that capture complex biological processes and cell-cell communication patterns. These latent representations can be extracted for downstream analysis, visualization in reduced-dimensional spaces, or mapped back to physical spatial coordinates. This functionality enables researchers to explore biological niches, identify gene programs associated with specific cell types or conditions, and generate publication-ready visualizations that integrate multiple layers of biological information.

## Latent Representation Extraction

The `get_latent_representation()` method extracts gene program scores (latent features) from a trained NicheCompass model. This function serves as the primary interface for accessing the compressed learned representations that capture biological signals in the data. The extraction process supports both deterministic latent features (z) and the probabilistic posterior distribution parameters (μ and σ), providing flexibility for different analytical needs.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L1264-L1382)

The extraction follows a systematic workflow. First, the method validates that the model has been trained and prepares the data using the same preprocessing pipeline employed during training. This ensures consistency between the training phase and extraction phase. For large datasets, the function implements batch processing to manage memory efficiently, processing data in configurable batch sizes while maintaining the integrity of the latent representations.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Start: get_latent_representation] --> B{Check if trained?}
    B -->|No| C[Error: Model must be trained]
    B -->|Yes| D[Set device<br/>GPU/CPU]
    D --> E[Prepare data with<br/>preprocessing pipeline]
    E --> F[Initialize dataloader<br/>with batch processing]
    F --> G{Return mu_std?}
    G -->|Yes| H[Initialize mu, std arrays]
    G -->|No| I[Initialize z array]
    H --> J[Process batches<br/>for each node_batch]
    I --> J
    J --> K[Model forward pass<br/>encoder only]
    K --> L[Extract latent from<br/>model.get_latent_representation]
    L --> M[Store in arrays<br/>detach & CPU transfer]
    M --> N{More batches?}
    N -->|Yes| J
    N -->|No| O[Return z or mu, std]
```

The method provides several key configuration options. The `only_active_gps` parameter controls whether to return representations only for gene programs that were identified as active during training (default: True) or for all gene programs including inactive ones. Active gene programs typically provide the most biologically relevant signals while reducing dimensionality. The `return_mu_std` parameter allows access to the variational posterior distribution parameters instead of the sampled latent variable z, which is useful for uncertainty quantification or probabilistic analyses. The `node_batch_size` parameter (default: 64) enables memory-efficient processing of large spatial datasets by processing nodes in batches.

The function returns numpy arrays with dimensions (n_obs × n_gps), where each row represents a cell and each column represents a gene program activity score. These latent representations serve as inputs for downstream visualization and analysis tasks.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L1264-L1382)

> [!TIP]
> When extracting latent representations for new data (not the training data), ensure that the same preprocessing parameters (counts_key, adj_key, cat_covariates_keys) are used as during training to maintain compatibility with the learned model weights.

## Visualization of Gene Program Activities

NicheCompass provides comprehensive visualization capabilities through the `generate_enriched_gp_info_plots()` function, which creates multi-panel visualizations integrating enriched category information, gene program activity scores, and the expression patterns of top contributing genes or peaks. This function is particularly valuable for interpreting the biological significance of gene programs identified through differential testing.

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L212-L420)

The visualization framework supports multiple feature spaces. The default latent space uses UMAP embeddings computed from the gene program activity scores to show global patterns and relationships between cells. Alternatively, spatial feature spaces can be used by specifying sample identifiers from `adata.obs`, which maps gene program activities back to physical coordinates in the spatial transcriptomics data. This dual-view approach enables researchers to understand both the abstract structure of the latent space and the spatial organization of gene program activities.

The function generates comprehensive info plots with the following panel structure for each gene program:

| Panel | Content | Purpose |
|-------|---------|---------|
| 1 | Enriched category (cell type/condition) | Shows which category the GP is enriched in |
| 2 | Gene program activity scores | Displays spatial or latent distribution of GP activity |
| 3+ | Top contributing genes/peaks | Shows expression of the most important features for each GP |

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L406-L632)

The visualization configuration is highly customizable. Users can specify the number of top enriched gene programs to visualize using `n_top_enriched_gp_start_idx` and `n_top_enriched_gp_end_idx` parameters. The `n_top_genes_per_gp` and `n_top_peaks_per_gp` parameters control how many of the most important contributing features (genes for RNA data, peaks for ATAC-seq data) are displayed for each gene program. The `feature_spaces` parameter accepts a list that can include "latent" for UMAP visualizations or sample names from `adata.obs[sample_key]` for spatial visualizations, allowing users to generate plots in multiple views simultaneously.

Color mapping is intelligently handled based on the biological context. Enriched categories use a provided `cat_palette` dictionary for consistent coloring across all plots. Gene program activity scores use a diverging "RdBu" colormap (red-white-blue) to show positive and negative activations. Omics features use sequential colormaps—"Blues" for positively contributing genes and "Reds" for negatively contributing genes—making it easy to identify activation patterns. When `scale_omics_ft=True`, the function applies z-score scaling to genes and peaks and switches to a symmetric "RdBu" colormap, which is useful for comparing relative expression patterns across features.

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L212-L420)

> [!TIP]
> When visualizing gene programs in spatial coordinates, use the `spot_size` parameter to adjust point sizes based on your data density. Larger datasets or higher-resolution spatial data typically benefit from smaller spot sizes to prevent overlapping points.

## Integration with Spatial Data

The visualization framework seamlessly integrates latent representations with spatial transcriptomics data through scanpy's plotting infrastructure. This integration enables researchers to map abstract gene program activities back to their physical locations within tissues, revealing spatial patterns of biological processes and cell-cell communication.

For spatial visualizations, the function filters the AnnData object to cells from a specific sample (`adata[adata.obs[sample_key] == feature_space]`) and generates spatial scatter plots using `sc.pl.spatial()`. The `spot_size` parameter controls the size of each cell representation in the plot, which should be adjusted based on tissue density and the desired level of visual detail. The gene program activity scores are extracted from `adata.obs` and displayed using a continuous color scale that highlights regions of high and low activity.

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L506-L532)

The spatial plotting workflow supports both the original expression data and the derived gene program scores. For genes and peaks, the function plots the original expression or accessibility counts. This provides a direct view of the input data that contributed to the gene program activation. The use of directional colormaps (Blues for positive contributions, Reds for negative contributions) helps researchers quickly identify which features are driving the observed spatial patterns of gene program activity.

When working with multi-sample datasets or spatial atlases, the ability to visualize gene programs across multiple samples provides insights into conserved and sample-specific patterns. The `generate_enriched_gp_info_plots()` function accepts multiple feature spaces, enabling generation of visualizations for both the latent UMAP (showing global relationships) and each individual spatial sample (showing local spatial organization) in a single function call.

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L212-L420)

## Workflow Example: Extracting and Visualizing Gene Programs

A typical workflow for extracting and visualizing latent representations involves several sequential steps. After training the model, researchers extract the latent representations for analysis, visualize them in reduced-dimensional space, and optionally map them back to spatial coordinates. This workflow enables interpretation of the learned gene programs and their biological relevance.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Train NicheCompass Model] --> B[Run Differential GP Tests]
    B --> C[Extract Latent<br/>Representations]
    C --> D[Compute Gene/Peak<br/>Importances for GPs]
    D --> E[Generate Visualizations]
    E --> F{Visualization Type?}
    F -->|Latent Space| G[UMAP plots showing<br/>GP activities and categories]
    F -->|Spatial| H[Spatial plots showing<br/>GP activity patterns]
    F -->|Combined| I[Multi-panel info plots<br/>with top contributing features]
```

The practical implementation involves calling the appropriate methods in sequence. First, latent representations are extracted using `model.get_latent_representation()` and stored in `adata.obsm[latent_key]`. These representations can then be used to compute UMAP embeddings using scanpy's standard dimensionality reduction functions. For spatial visualizations, the gene program scores are already accessible in `adata.obs` after extraction and can be directly plotted using the visualization functions.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L1264-L1382), [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L212-L420)

The visualization generation requires specification of the differential testing results key to identify which gene programs are enriched for different categories. The `cat_palette` parameter provides consistent color mappings for categories across all visualizations. By adjusting the range of enriched gene programs (via `n_top_enriched_gp_start_idx` and `n_top_enriched_gp_end_idx`), researchers can focus on the most statistically significant programs or explore additional candidates.

For comprehensive analysis, researchers typically generate visualizations in both latent and spatial feature spaces. The latent space view reveals global relationships and clustering patterns, while spatial views show the physical organization of gene program activities. Together, these perspectives provide a complete understanding of how gene programs organize in both abstract and physical dimensions.

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L212-L420)

## Parameter Configuration Guide

Successful latent representation extraction and visualization requires appropriate parameter selection based on dataset characteristics and analysis goals. The following table summarizes key parameters and their recommended usage scenarios.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L1264-L1382), [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L212-L420)

| Parameter | Type | Default | Recommended Usage |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------------|
| `only_active_gps` | bool | True | Use True for most analyses; set to False only when comparing inactive programs |
| `return_mu_std` | bool | False | Set True for uncertainty quantification or probabilistic analyses |
| `node_batch_size` | int | 64 | Increase for large datasets (>100k cells) to balance memory and speed |
| `dtype` | type | np.float64 | Use np.float32 for memory efficiency with very large datasets |
| `feature_spaces` | list | ["latent"] | Include sample names for spatial views alongside "latent" |
| `n_top_genes_per_gp` | int | 3 | Increase (5-10) for deeper biological interpretation |
| `n_top_peaks_per_gp` | int | 0 | Set >0 only for multi-modal models with ATAC data |
| `scale_omics_ft` | bool | False | Set True when comparing relative expression patterns |
| `spot_size` | float | 30. | Adjust based on spatial data density (10-100 range) |

For large-scale datasets (>500k cells), increasing `node_batch_size` to 256 or 512 can significantly improve extraction speed while using moderate memory. When memory is constrained, using `dtype=np.float32` reduces memory requirements by 50% with minimal impact on visualization quality. The `feature_spaces` parameter should be customized based on analysis needs—include both "latent" and spatial sample IDs when generating comprehensive multi-view reports.


# Differential Gene Program Testing



Differential Gene Program Testing is a statistical analysis method that identifies which gene programs are differentially active across biological categories in spatial transcriptomics data. This capability enables researchers to discover biological processes that distinguish cell types, disease states, tissue regions, or experimental conditions by comparing gene program activity scores computed from the trained NicheCompass model. The analysis leverages Bayesian statistical methods to quantify the evidence for enrichment, providing both statistical significance (p-values) and strength of evidence (log Bayes Factors).

## Statistical Foundations and Hypothesis Testing

The differential testing framework implements a Bayesian hypothesis comparison approach rather than traditional frequentist statistics. For each gene program and category pair, the method compares two competing hypotheses:

- **Hypothesis H0**: The normalized gene program/latent scores of observations in the category under consideration (z₀) are higher than the normalized scores of observations in the comparison categories (z₁)
- **Hypothesis H1**: The normalized gene program/latent scores of comparison category observations (z₁) are higher than or equal to the scores of the category under consideration (z₀)

The log Bayes Factor quantifies the strength of evidence supporting H₀ over H₁. Higher positive values indicate stronger evidence that the gene program is enriched in the category of interest. The implementation adapts methodology from scArches, establishing continuity with established best practices in single-cell gene program analysis [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L830-L872).

The statistical computation uses probability calculations based on the complementary error function (erfc), which provides numerical stability when comparing distributions. For each gene program comparison:

```
to_reduce = - (z₀ - z₁) / √(2(σ₀² + σ₁²))
p_h0 = mean(0.5 × erfc(to_reduce))
p_h1 = 1.0 - p_h0
log_bayes_factor = log(p_h0 + ε) - log(p_h1 + ε)
```

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L973-L988)

## Differential Testing Workflow

The differential gene program testing process follows a structured workflow that integrates with the trained NicheCompass model's latent representations. This workflow enables systematic comparison of gene program activities across predefined biological categories.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Start Differential Testing] --> B[Retrieve Active Gene Programs]
    B --> C[Get Latent Representations]
    C --> D[Extract Category Labels]
    D --> E[For Each Selected Category]
    E --> F[Identify Comparison Categories]
    F --> G[Sample n_obs from Each Group]
    G --> H[Compute Log Bayes Factors]
    H --> I[Filter by Threshold]
    I --> J{More Categories?}
    J -->|Yes| E
    J -->|No| K[Compile Results DataFrame]
    K --> L[Store Results in adata.uns]
    L --> M[Add Enriched GP Scores to adata.obs]
    M --> N[Return Enriched Gene Programs]
    
    style A fill:#e3f2fd
    style N fill:#4caf50
    style H fill:#fff3e0
```

The workflow begins by extracting active gene programs and computing latent representations from the trained model. For each category under investigation, the method systematically compares against specified comparison groups, performs statistical testing using the log Bayes Factor metric, and aggregates results into a structured DataFrame for downstream analysis and visualization.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L830-L1052)

## Core Parameters and Configuration

The `run_differential_gp_tests` method provides extensive configuration options to tailor the analysis to specific research questions and data characteristics.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `cat_key` | str | required | Key in `adata.obs` storing category labels for comparison |
| `selected_cats` | str/list | None | Categories to test (None = all categories in column) |
| `comparison_cats` | str/list | "rest" | Comparison groups ("rest" = all other categories) |
| `selected_gps` | str/list | None | Gene programs to test (None = all active programs) |
| `n_sample` | int | 10000 | Number of observations sampled per group for computation |
| `log_bayes_factor_thresh` | float | 2.3 | Threshold for considering gene programs enriched |
| `key_added` | str | "nichecompass_differential_gp_test_results" | Storage key in `adata.uns` |
| `seed` | int | 0 | Random seed for reproducible sampling |
| `adata` | AnnData | None | AnnData object (None = uses model's stored adata) |

The default log Bayes Factor threshold of 2.3 corresponds to "strong evidence" according to conventional Bayesian interpretation scales. This threshold balances sensitivity (detecting true differences) with specificity (avoiding false positives). Researchers may adjust this threshold based on their specific requirements: lower thresholds for exploratory analysis to identify candidate patterns, higher thresholds for confirmatory analysis requiring stronger evidence.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L830-L873)

> [!TIP]
> When using `"rest"` as the comparison category, each category is compared against all other categories combined. For pairwise comparisons between specific categories, provide the exact category names in the `comparison_cats` parameter. This enables more focused biological questions (e.g., comparing disease subtypes against healthy controls).

## Results Structure and Interpretation

The differential testing results are stored as a structured pandas DataFrame in `adata.uns[key_added]`, containing comprehensive statistical information for each category-gene program pair that exceeds the enrichment threshold.

### Results DataFrame Columns

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `category` | The biological category under investigation |
| `gene_program` | Name of the gene program tested |
| `p_h0` | Probability that category scores > comparison scores |
| `p_h1` | Probability that comparison scores >= category scores |
| `log_bayes_factor` | Log Bayes Factor quantifying enrichment evidence |

The DataFrame is sorted by absolute log Bayes Factor in descending order, prioritizing the most strongly enriched gene programs for inspection. This ordering helps researchers focus on the most biologically significant findings first. In addition to the DataFrame, the method automatically adds the scores of all enriched gene programs to `adata.obs`, enabling immediate visualization and further analysis.

### Interpretation Guidelines

- **Log Bayes Factor > 2.3**: Strong evidence for enrichment in the category
- **Log Bayes Factor ≈ 0**: No substantial evidence for difference
- **Log Bayes Factor < -2.3**: Strong evidence for depletion in the category (relative to comparison)
- **p_h0 close to 1.0**: High probability the category has higher activity
- **p_h0 close to 0.0**: Low probability the category has higher activity

The method also handles edge cases robustly: if either group has zero activity for a gene program, the log Bayes Factor is set to 0 to avoid division by zero and ensure meaningful statistics only for programs with measurable activity.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L989-L1052)

## Implementation Details: Step-by-Step Walkthrough

### 1. Initial Setup and Validation

The method begins by verifying that the model has been trained and retrieving necessary components:

```python
self._check_if_trained(warn=True)
np.random.seed(seed)

# Get active gene programs
active_gps = list(adata.uns[self.active_gp_names_key_])
```

This validation step ensures statistical testing is only performed on models with learned representations. The random seed ensures reproducible results across multiple runs.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L909-L914)

### 2. Gene Program Selection and Latent Representation Extraction

For the selected gene programs (or all active programs if not specified), the method retrieves indices and weights, then computes latent representations:

```python
selected_gps_idx, selected_gps_weights, chrom_access_gp_weights = \
    self.get_gp_data(selected_gps=selected_gps)

mu, std = self.get_latent_representation(
    adata=adata,
    counts_key=self.counts_key_,
    adj_key=self.adj_key_,
    cat_covariates_keys=self.cat_covariates_keys_,
    only_active_gps=False,
    return_mu_std=True,
    node_batch_size=self.node_batch_size_)
mu_selected_gps = mu[:, selected_gps_idx]
std_selected_gps = std[:, selected_gps_idx]
```

The latent representation provides the gene program activity scores that serve as the basis for differential comparison. Setting `only_active_gp=False` ensures all relevant programs are included regardless of their training-time activation status.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L923-L937)

### 3. Category Identification and Masking

The method identifies all unique categories and creates boolean masks for the category of interest and comparison categories:

```python
cat_values = adata.obs[cat_key].replace(np.nan, "NaN")
cats = cat_values.unique()

cat_mask = cat_values == cat
if comparison_cats == "rest":
    comparison_cat_mask = ~cat_mask
else:
    comparison_cat_mask = cat_values.isin(comparison_cats)
```

The replacement of NaN values ensures proper handling of missing category labels. The masking strategy efficiently isolates observations for statistical comparison without creating subset copies of large arrays.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L939-L957)

### 4. Random Sampling for Statistical Computation

To ensure computational efficiency with large datasets, the method samples observations equally from both groups:

```python
cat_idx = np.random.choice(cat_mask.sum(), n_sample)
comparison_cat_idx = np.random.choice(comparison_cat_mask.sum(), n_sample)

mu_selected_gps_cat_sample = mu_selected_gps_cat[cat_idx]
std_selected_gps_cat_sample = std_selected_gps_cat[cat_idx]
mu_selected_gps_comparison_cat_sample = mu_selected_gps_comparison_cat[comparison_cat_idx]
std_selected_gps_comparison_cat_sample = std_selected_gps_comparison_cat[comparison_cat_idx]
```

This sampling strategy maintains statistical power while controlling computational cost, especially important for large spatial transcriptomics datasets with hundreds of thousands of observations.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L958-L967)

### 5. Log Bayes Factor Computation

The core statistical calculation computes the log Bayes Factor for each gene program:

```python
to_reduce = - (mu_selected_gps_cat_sample - mu_selected_gps_comparison_cat_sample) / \
             np.sqrt(2 * (std_selected_gps_cat_sample**2 + std_selected_gps_comparison_cat_sample**2))
to_reduce = 0.5 * erfc(to_reduce)
p_h0 = np.mean(to_reduce, axis=0)
p_h1 = 1.0 - p_h0
epsilon = 1e-12
log_bayes_factor = np.log(p_h0 + epsilon) - np.log(p_h1 + epsilon)
```

The epsilon term prevents numerical errors when probabilities approach zero. The use of `erfc` (complementary error function) provides stable numerical computation of the tail probabilities needed for the Bayesian hypothesis comparison.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L969-L988)

### 6. Results Compilation and Filtering

After computing statistics for all category-gene program pairs, the method compiles results into a DataFrame and filters for enriched programs:

```python
results = pd.DataFrame(results)
results["abs_log_bayes_factor"] = np.abs(results["log_bayes_factor"])
results = results[results["abs_log_bayes_factor"] > log_bayes_factor_thresh]
results.sort_values(by="abs_log_bayes_factor", ascending=False, inplace=True)
results.reset_index(drop=True, inplace=True)
results.drop("abs_log_bayes_factor", axis=1, inplace=True)
adata.uns[key_added] = results
```

The filtering step ensures only biologically meaningful differences are retained in the final results, reducing noise and focusing interpretation on the most relevant findings.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L995-L1005)

### 7. Enriched Program Score Storage

For visualization and downstream analysis, the method adds scores of enriched gene programs to the AnnData object:

```python
enriched_gps = results["gene_program"].unique().tolist()
enriched_gps_idx = [selected_gps.index(gp) for gp in enriched_gps]

enriched_gps_gp_scores = pd.DataFrame(
    mu_selected_gps[:, enriched_gps_idx],
    columns=enriched_gps,
    index=adata.obs.index)
new_cols = [col for col in enriched_gps_gp_scores.columns 
            if col not in adata.obs.columns]
if new_cols:
    adata.obs = pd.concat([adata.obs, enriched_gps_gp_scores[new_cols]], axis=1)
```

This integration enables immediate spatial visualization of gene program activities using standard scanpy plotting functions, facilitating biological interpretation and hypothesis generation.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L1006-L1052)

## Visualization of Enriched Gene Programs

The `generate_enriched_gp_info_plots` function creates comprehensive visualizations of the top enriched gene programs, displaying spatial patterns of gene program activity alongside the expression of their constituent genes and peaks.

### Visualization Components

The function generates multi-panel visualizations showing:
- **Enriched category label** identifying which category shows enrichment
- **Gene program activity scores** displayed in the specified feature space (latent or physical space)
- **Top gene expression** showing the most important genes in the program
- **Top peak accessibility** (for ATAC models) showing chromatin accessibility patterns

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Input: Model & Test Results] --> B[Extract Top Enriched GPs]
    B --> C[Compute GP Gene Importances]
    C --> D[Identify Top Genes per GP]
    D --> E[For ATAC: Compute Peak Importances]
    E --> F[For Each Feature Space]
    F --> G[Generate Spatial Plots]
    G --> H[Activity Scores + Gene/Peak Expression]
    H --> I[Save or Display Figures]
```

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L212-L405)

### Visualization Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| `n_top_enriched_gp_start_idx` | 0 | Starting index of top enriched programs |
| `n_top_enriched_gp_end_idx` | 10 | Ending index of top enriched programs |
| `feature_spaces` | ["latent"] | Feature spaces for visualization |
| `n_top_genes_per_gp` | 3 | Number of top genes to display per program |
| `n_top_peaks_per_gp` | 0 | Number of top peaks to display (ATAC only) |
| `scale_omics_ft` | False | Whether to scale gene/peak counts |

The flexibility in feature space selection allows researchers to visualize gene program activities either in the learned latent space or in the original physical spatial coordinates, depending on their analytical needs.

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L212-L230)

> [!TIP]
> Set `scale_omics_ft=True` when working with counts that span multiple orders of magnitude. This scaling improves visualization of subtle expression patterns by normalizing the color scale across all genes/peaks. Use the default `False` when working with log-normalized data or when absolute differences are biologically meaningful.

## Advanced Features and Considerations

### Multiple Testing Considerations

The method uses a Bayesian framework with log Bayes Factors rather than traditional frequentist p-values, which inherently addresses multiple testing through the Bayesian prior structure. However, researchers should still consider the exploratory nature of the analysis and validate key findings through orthogonal methods.

### Missing Data Handling

Categories with missing values in the `cat_key` column are handled by replacing NaN with "NaN" as a distinct category. This ensures observations with missing labels are excluded from comparisons rather than causing errors in the statistical computation.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L939)

### Computational Performance

The computational complexity scales linearly with the number of categories, gene programs, and the `n_sample` parameter. For large-scale analyses with many categories and gene programs:
- Use moderate `n_sample` values (5000-10000) for initial exploration
- Restrict `selected_cats` and `selected_gps` to hypotheses of primary interest
- Consider running analyses in parallel for independent category comparisons

### Integration with Spatial Analysis

Differential gene program testing seamlessly integrates with NicheCompass's spatial analysis capabilities. The enriched gene program scores stored in `adata.obs` can be used with scanpy's spatial plotting functions to visualize spatial patterns of differential activity. This integration enables researchers to map enriched biological programs back to tissue architecture, revealing spatial heterogeneity in molecular processes.

For more advanced spatial characterization, the enriched gene programs identified through differential testing can be further analyzed using niche characterization methods described in [Niche Characterization and Gene Importance Computation](25-niche-characterization-and-gene-importance-computation).

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L1029-L1052)

## Common Use Cases and Applications

### Cell Type Marker Discovery

Identify gene programs that distinguish specific cell types from all others:
```python
model.run_differential_gp_tests(
    cat_key="cell_type",
    selected_cats="T_cells",
    comparison_cats="rest"
)
```

### Disease vs. Normal Comparison

Compare disease states against healthy controls to identify disease-associated pathways:

model.run_differential_gp_tests(
    cat_key="disease_status",
    selected_cats="AD",  # Alzheimer's disease
    comparison_cats="Normal"
)
```

### Regional Spatial Analysis

Identify gene programs enriched in specific anatomical regions:

model.run_differential_gp_tests(
    cat_key="anatomical_region",
    selected_cats=["Hippocampus", "Cortex"],
    comparison_cats="rest",
    n_sample=15000
)
```

### Treatment Response Analysis

Compare treated and untreated samples to identify responsive pathways:
```python
model.run_differential_gp_tests(
    cat_key="treatment",
    selected_cats="drug_treated",
    comparison_cats="vehicle_control",
    selected_gps=["pathway1", "pathway2", "pathway3"]
)
```

These use cases demonstrate how differential gene program testing provides a flexible framework for hypothesis-driven biological discovery across diverse experimental designs and research questions.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L830-L873)

## Best Practices and Recommendations

### Parameter Selection Guidelines

1. **Sampling Size (`n_sample`)**: Use 10,000 for comprehensive analysis, 5,000 for faster exploratory work. Larger samples improve statistical stability at the cost of computation time.

2. **Log Bayes Factor Threshold**: 
   - 2.3: Standard "strong evidence" threshold (recommended)
   - 3.0: More stringent for high-confidence findings
   - 1.5: More permissive for exploratory analysis

3. **Category Selection**: Start with broad comparisons (category vs. "rest") to identify general patterns, then refine to specific pairwise comparisons for focused investigation.

4. **Gene Program Selection**: When using prior knowledge gene programs, include programs from multiple pathways to ensure comprehensive coverage of biological processes. For exploratory analyses with learned programs, include all active programs to discover novel associations.

### Validation Strategies

- **Cross-dataset validation**: Test whether enriched gene programs replicate across independent biological replicates or similar datasets
- **Spatial consistency**: Verify that enriched programs show coherent spatial patterns consistent with known biology
- **Gene-level validation**: Examine expression of individual genes in enriched programs to confirm expected patterns

### Integration with Downstream Analyses

Differential gene program testing results can inform several downstream analyses:

- **Cell-cell communication**: Use enriched programs as seeds for communication network analysis in [Cell-Cell Communication Network Analysis](24-cell-cell-communication-network-analysis)
- **Latent visualization**: Project enriched programs onto latent space visualizations from [Latent Representation Extraction and Visualization](22-latent-representation-extraction-and-visualization)
- **Benchmarking**: Compare differential testing performance with other methods using [Benchmarking and Model Evaluation](26-benchmarking-and-model-evaluation)

## Troubleshooting and Common Issues

### No Enriched Gene Programs Found

**Symptoms**: Results DataFrame is empty or contains very few entries.

**Possible Causes**:
- Log Bayes Factor threshold too high for effect sizes in data
- Categories may not have substantial biological differences
- Gene programs may not be relevant to the biological question

**Solutions**:
- Lower the `log_bayes_factor_thresh` parameter (e.g., to 1.5 or 2.0)
- Verify category labels and ensure meaningful differences exist
- Consider different gene program selections or prior knowledge sources

### Computational Performance Issues

**Symptoms**: Long computation times for large datasets.

**Possible Causes**:
- Large number of categories or gene programs being tested
- High `n_sample` parameter
- Large AnnData objects with many observations

**Solutions**:
- Reduce `n_sample` parameter (e.g., to 5,000)
- Test a subset of categories using `selected_cats`
- Test a subset of gene programs using `selected_gps`

### Unexpected Categories in Results

**Symptoms**: Categories not in `selected_cats` appear in results.

**Possible Causes**: The method only tests categories not present in `comparison_cats`. When using `"rest"` as comparison, all categories except the current one are used as comparison.

**Solutions**: This is expected behavior for enrichment analysis. To test specific category pairs, provide exact category names in both `selected_cats` and `comparison_cats`.


# Cell-Cell Communication Network Analysis



Cell-cell communication (CCC) network analysis in NicheCompass enables the systematic inference and visualization of intercellular signaling events between spatially proximate cell types based on gene program activity. This advanced analytical framework integrates spatial transcriptomics data with gene program priors to reconstruct directed communication networks that capture the strength and specificity of molecular interactions between different cellular populations. The analysis leverages the learned latent representations from the VGPGAE model to quantify communication potential scores, which are then aggregated at the cell-type or niche level to reveal population-level communication patterns.

The CCC network analysis workflow operates on the fundamental premise that effective intercellular signaling requires both spatial proximity and molecular compatibility—specifically, the co-expression of ligand-receptor gene pairs or coordinated activity of signaling pathway gene programs in neighboring cells. By modeling this interaction through learned gene program weights and spatial neighborhood graphs, NicheCompass provides a biologically interpretable framework for hypothesis generation about cellular crosstalk mechanisms in complex tissue microenvironments.

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L871-L1012), [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L1689-L1987)

## Computational Methodology

The CCC network computation implements a multi-stage pipeline that transforms raw spatial transcriptomics data and model outputs into interpretable communication networks. The core algorithmic framework begins by computing individual cell-level communication potential scores for each gene program of interest, then integrates these scores with spatial neighborhood information to derive cell-pair communication strengths, and finally aggregates and normalizes these strengths to produce population-level network representations.

### Cell-Level Communication Potential Scoring

For each gene program in the analysis set, the algorithm computes two complementary scores per cell: a source score and a target score. The source score quantifies a cell's capacity to send signals based on its expression of source genes (ligands, secreted factors) weighted by the gene program's learned source gene importance parameters. Conversely, the target score quantifies a cell's receptivity to signals based on expression of target genes (receptors, downstream effectors) weighted by the gene program's learned target gene importance parameters. These scores are computed as the normalized product of gene expression levels, GP activation scores from the latent representation, and learned decoder weights.

The mathematical formulation for source and target scores follows: for cell i and gene program gp, the source score is computed as `source_score[i] = mean_j(exp_gene[i,j] / max_exp[j] * weight_source[j] * gp_activation[i])` where j indexes source genes in the gene program. An analogous computation is performed for target scores using target gene weights. This formulation ensures that high scores require both appropriate gene expression and active gene program participation in that cell.

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L941-L975)

### Spatial Integration and Cell-Pair Strength Calculation

Once individual cell scores are computed, the algorithm integrates spatial context by identifying spatial neighborhoods through k-nearest neighbor graph construction. Using the spatial coordinates from `adata.obs['spatial']`, a KNN graph is computed with a default of 90 neighbors, stored under the `spatial_cci` key in `adata.obsp`. This graph defines the allowable communication pairs, respecting physical proximity constraints that are essential for paracrine and juxtacrine signaling.

Cell-pair communication strengths are calculated by taking the dot product of source and target score vectors, which inherently captures the intuition that strong communication requires both an active signal sender and an active signal receiver. This product is then element-wise multiplied with the spatial connectivity matrix to restrict communication to physically adjacent cells. The resulting sparse matrix contains pair-wise communication strengths for all spatially proximate cell pairs.

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L976-L988)

### Population-Level Aggregation and Normalization

To transform cell-level communication strengths into interpretable population-level networks, the algorithm aggregates scores using the `aggregate_obsp_matrix_per_cell_type` utility function. This function performs two key operations: first, it aggregates communication strengths by summing values for each cell type combination, creating a cell-type × cell-type matrix where each entry represents the total communication strength between that pair; second, it can optionally apply group-level filtering to focus on specific sample conditions or experimental groups.

The resulting aggregated values are then normalized to a [0, 1] range using min-max scaling: `normalized_strength = (strength - min_value) / (max_value - min_value)`. This normalization enables comparability across gene programs and facilitates visualization by mapping all communication strengths to a common scale. The final output is a pandas DataFrame with columns for source, target, normalized strength, unscaled strength, and edge type (gene program identifier).

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L989-L1012), [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L23-L104)

## Architecture and Data Flow

The CCC network analysis implements a sophisticated computational pipeline that coordinates multiple data sources and algorithmic components to transform raw measurements into biologically interpretable communication networks.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Input["Input Data"]
        A["Spatial Coordinates<br/>adata.obs['spatial']"]
        B["Gene Expression<br/>adata.X"]
        C["GP Activation<br/>adata.obsm[latent_key]"]
        D["GP Summary<br/>model.get_gp_summary()"]
    end
    
    subgraph Algorithm["Algorithm Stages"]
        E["Gene Program Selection<br/>gp_list"]
        F["Source/Target Score<br/>Computation"]
        G["Spatial KNN Graph<br/>n_neighbors=90"]
        H["Cell-Pair Strength<br/>Dot Product"]
        I["Aggregation by Cell Type<br/>group_key"]
        J["Normalization<br/>Min-Max Scaling"]
    end
    
    subgraph Output["Output Products"]
        K["Network DataFrame<br/>source, target, strength, edge_type"]
        L["Visualization<br/>Circular Network Plot"]
    end
    
    A --> G
    B --> F
    C --> F
    D --> F
    E --> F
    F --> H
    G --> H
    H --> I
    I --> J
    J --> K
    K --> L
    
    style A fill:#e3f2fd
    style B fill:#e3f2fd
    style C fill:#e3f2fd
    style D fill:#e3f2fd
    style K fill:#c8e6c9
    style L fill:#c8e6c9
```

The architecture demonstrates how spatial information, expression data, and learned model parameters converge through the algorithm to produce communication networks. Key design decisions include the use of sparse matrix operations for computational efficiency, normalization for cross-program comparability, and modular aggregation functions that support flexible grouping strategies.

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L871-L1012), [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L1689-L1987)

## Gene Program Summary Integration

The CCC analysis fundamentally relies on gene program summary information extracted from the trained model via the `get_gp_summary()` method. This method retrieves comprehensive metadata about each gene program, including source and target gene assignments, learned decoder weights, and importance scores. The summary DataFrame provides the critical weight vectors that modulate how much each gene contributes to communication potential for its associated gene program.

The GP summary contains several key fields: `gp_source_genes` and `gp_target_genes` (lists of gene names), `gp_source_genes_weights` and `gp_target_genes_weights` (learned decoder weights), and corresponding importance scores. These weights represent the model's learned understanding of which genes are most relevant for each gene program's signaling activity, with higher absolute weights indicating greater biological importance in the context of that program.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L1689-L1987)

## Implementation and Usage

### Computing Communication Networks

The primary entry point for CCC analysis is the `compute_communication_gp_network()` function, which requires a trained NicheCompass model and a list of gene programs to analyze. The function signature includes parameters for controlling spatial neighborhood size, aggregation grouping, and filtering options.

**Basic usage example:**

```python
from nichecompass.utils import compute_communication_gp_network

# Define gene programs of interest
gp_list = ['WNT_SIGNALING', 'TGF_BETA_PATHWAY', 'NOTCH_SIGNALING']

# Compute communication network
network_df = compute_communication_gp_network(
    gp_list=gp_list,
    model=model,
    group_key='niche',  # Aggregate by niche rather than cell type
    n_neighbors=90      # Spatial neighborhood size
)

# Output structure:
# network_df columns: ['source', 'target', 'strength', 'strength_unscaled', 'edge_type']
```

The function returns a pandas DataFrame where each row represents a directed communication edge between cell types or niches, with the strength indicating the normalized communication intensity and edge_type identifying the associated gene program.

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L871-L1012)

### Parameter Configuration Options

The CCC network computation supports several configurable parameters that influence the analysis scope and output structure:

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `gp_list` | list | required | List of gene program names for which to compute communication strengths |
| `model` | NicheCompass | required | Trained NicheCompass model instance |
| `group_key` | str | "niche" | Key in `adata.obs` defining aggregation groups (cell types, niches, etc.) |
| `filter_key` | Optional[str] | None | Optional key for additional filtering (e.g., sample condition) |
| `filter_cat` | Optional[str] | None | Category value for filtering when `filter_key` is specified |
| `n_neighbors` | int | 90 | Number of neighbors for spatial KNN graph construction |

The `group_key` parameter is particularly important, as it determines the granularity of the resulting network. Using `'cell_type'` produces traditional cell-type level communication networks, while using `'niche'` produces niche-to-niche communication networks that may reveal higher-order organizational principles in the tissue.

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L871-L913)

### Filtering and Subsetting

The analysis framework supports flexible filtering options to focus on specific biological contexts or experimental conditions. By specifying `filter_key` and `filter_cat`, users can compute communication networks for specific sample groups or tissue regions without recomputing the full spatial graph.

**Example: Condition-specific analysis**

```python
# Compute communication only for tumor samples
tumor_network = compute_communication_gp_network(
    gp_list=gp_list,
    model=model,
    group_key='cell_type',
    filter_key='condition',  # Column with condition labels
    filter_cat='tumor',      # Only analyze tumor samples
    n_neighbors=90
)

# Compute communication only for normal samples
normal_network = compute_communication_gp_network(
    gp_list=gp_list,
    model=model,
    group_key='cell_type',
    filter_key='condition',
    filter_cat='normal',
    n_neighbors=90
)
```

This capability enables comparative analysis of communication patterns across different biological conditions, which is valuable for identifying condition-specific signaling alterations in disease states.

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L891-L892), [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L989-L992)

## Visualization and Interpretation

### Network Visualization

The `visualize_communication_gp_network()` function provides sophisticated visualization capabilities for communication networks using circular layouts that clearly display directed communication flows between cell types or niches. The visualization uses NetworkX's circular layout algorithm combined with matplotlib customization to produce publication-quality figures.

**Basic visualization example:**

```python
from nichecompass.utils import visualize_communication_gp_network

# Define colors for each cell type/niche
cat_colors = {
    'Niche_A': '#1f77b4',
    'Niche_B': '#ff7f0e',
    'Niche_C': '#2ca02c',
    'Niche_D': '#d62728'
}

# Visualize the network
visualize_communication_gp_network(
    adata=model.adata,
    network_df=network_df,
    cat_colors=cat_colors,
    edge_width_scale=20.0,      # Scale edge thickness by strength
    node_size=500,
    fontsize=14,
    figsize=(18, 16),
    plot_legend=True,
    save=True,
    save_path='communication_network.svg',
    cat_key='niche'
)
```

The visualization uses several visual encodings: edge thickness represents communication strength (scaled by `edge_width_scale`), edge colors distinguish different gene programs, and node positions follow a circular layout with radiating connections that maintain directional information.

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L1014-L1148)

### Visualization Customization Options

The visualization function supports extensive customization through parameters controlling layout, styling, and output formatting:

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `edge_type_colors` | Optional[dict] | None | Custom color scheme for gene programs (default: colorblind-optimized vega_10) |
| `edge_width_scale` | float | 20.0 | Scaling factor for edge thickness based on strength |
| `node_size` | int | 500 | Size of network nodes |
| `fontsize` | int | 14 | Font size for node labels |
| `figsize` | Tuple[int, int] | (18, 16) | Figure dimensions |
| `plot_legend` | bool | True | Whether to display the legend |
| `connection_style` | str | "arc3, rad = 0.1" | Matplotlib connection style for edges |
| `edge_attr` | str | "strength" | Network edge attribute to use for visualization |

The default edge color scheme uses a colorblind-optimized palette derived from Vega 10 with modifications from Scanpy, ensuring accessibility for viewers with color vision deficiencies. Users can provide custom color dictionaries to match publication requirements or thematic consistency across figures.

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L1034-L1066)

### Chord Diagram Alternative

For alternative visualization approaches, users can employ the `create_cell_type_chord_plot_from_df()` function to generate chord diagrams that display bidirectional communication flows in a circular format. This is particularly useful when emphasizing reciprocal communication relationships or when the network density makes directed edge visualization cluttered.

```python
from nichecompass.utils import create_cell_type_chord_plot_from_df

# Create chord diagram
create_cell_type_chord_plot_from_df(
    adata=model.adata,
    df=network_df,  # Communication network DataFrame
    link_threshold=0.01,  # Minimum strength to display
    cell_type_key='niche',
    plot_label='Gene Program Communication',
    save_fig=True,
    file_path='communication_chord.png'
)
```

Chord diagrams provide a complementary perspective by explicitly showing the magnitude of bidirectional communication between pairs, which can reveal symmetric or asymmetric signaling relationships that might be less obvious in directed network plots.

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L105-L211)

## Advanced Analysis Patterns

### Comparative Communication Analysis

A powerful application of CCC network analysis is comparing communication patterns across different biological conditions, developmental stages, or treatment groups. This comparative approach can reveal condition-specific signaling alterations that may underlie disease mechanisms or treatment responses.

The workflow typically involves computing separate networks for each condition of interest, then performing differential analysis on edge strengths to identify significantly altered communication pathways.

```python
# Compute networks for multiple conditions
conditions = ['control', 'treatment_A', 'treatment_B']
networks = {}

for condition in conditions:
    networks[condition] = compute_communication_gp_network(
        gp_list=gp_list,
        model=model,
        group_key='cell_type',
        filter_key='condition',
        filter_cat=condition
    )

# Identify differential communication
for gp in gp_list:
    for source in networks['control']['source'].unique():
        for target in networks['control']['target'].unique():
            control_strength = networks['control'][
                (networks['control']['source'] == source) & 
                (networks['control']['target'] == target) &
                (networks['control']['edge_type'] == gp)
            ]['strength'].values[0] if len(networks['control'][
                (networks['control']['source'] == source) & 
                (networks['control']['target'] == target) &
                (networks['control']['edge_type'] == gp)
            ]) > 0 else 0
            
            treatment_strength = networks['treatment_A'][
                (networks['treatment_A']['source'] == source) & 
                (networks['treatment_A']['target'] == target) &
                (networks['treatment_A']['edge_type'] == gp)
            ]['strength'].values[0] if len(networks['treatment_A'][
                (networks['treatment_A']['source'] == source) & 
                (networks['treatment_A']['target'] == target) &
                (networks['treatment_A']['edge_type'] == gp)
            ]) > 0 else 0
            
            fold_change = (treatment_strength + 1e-6) / (control_strength + 1e-6)
            # Analyze fold changes to identify altered communication
```

This pattern enables systematic identification of communication pathways that are upregulated or downregulated in response to experimental perturbations, providing mechanistic insights into cellular responses.

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L871-L1012)

### Multi-Scale Communication Analysis

The CCC framework supports analysis at multiple organizational scales by changing the `group_key` parameter. This multi-scale perspective can reveal communication patterns that are consistent across scales or that emerge only at specific levels of organization.

```python
# Compute communication at different scales
scales = {
    'cell_type': model.adata.obs['cell_type'],
    'niche': model.adata.obs['niche'],
    'region': model.adata.obs['region']
}

scale_networks = {}
for scale_name, scale_key in scales.items():
    scale_networks[scale_name] = compute_communication_gp_network(
        gp_list=gp_list,
        model=model,
        group_key=scale_key,
        n_neighbors=90
    )

# Compare communication patterns across scales
for scale_name, network_df in scale_networks.items():
    print(f"\n{scale_name} scale communication:")
    print(network_df.groupby('edge_type')['strength'].agg(['mean', 'max', 'count']))
```

Multi-scale analysis is particularly valuable for understanding how local cell-cell interactions propagate to tissue-level organization, enabling the identification of conserved communication motifs across organizational hierarchies.

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L891-L892)

### Integration with Differential GP Testing

CCC network analysis can be integrated with differential gene program testing to understand how changes in gene program activity relate to altered communication patterns. This combined approach provides a comprehensive view of both the signaling molecules and the communication pathways that are altered in different conditions.

```python
# Run differential GP testing
diff_results = model.run_differential_gp_tests(
    cat_key='condition',
    selected_cats=['tumor'],
    comparison_cats='normal',
    log_bayes_factor_thresh=2.3
)

# Extract significantly differentially active GPs
signif_gps = diff_results['nichecompass_differential_gp_test_results'][
    diff_results['nichecompass_differential_gp_test_results']['log_bayes_factor'] > 2.3
]['gp_name'].unique()

# Compute communication networks for significant GPs
signif_network = compute_communication_gp_network(
    gp_list=signif_gps.tolist(),
    model=model,
    group_key='cell_type',
    filter_key='condition',
    filter_cat='tumor'
)

# Visualize condition-specific communication
visualize_communication_gp_network(
    adata=model.adata,
    network_df=signif_network,
    cat_colors=cat_colors,
    plot_label='Tumor-Specific Communication',
    save_path='tumor_communication.svg'
)
```

This integrated analysis identifies communication pathways mediated by gene programs that are differentially active in the condition of interest, directly linking molecular activity changes to cellular communication alterations.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L830-L840), [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L871-L1012)

## Performance Considerations

### Computational Complexity

The CCC network computation involves several computationally intensive steps, particularly for large datasets with many cells and gene programs. The main computational bottlenecks include: (1) spatial KNN graph construction, which scales as O(n log n) for n cells; (2) source and target score computation, which scales as O(n × g × m) where g is the number of genes per program and m is the number of gene programs; and (3) sparse matrix operations for cell-pair strength computation, which scales with the number of edges in the spatial graph.

To optimize performance, the implementation employs sparse matrix operations throughout and caches the spatial KNN graph when possible. The function checks whether a pre-computed graph exists with the same `n_neighbors` parameter and reuses it to avoid redundant computation. For very large datasets, users may consider reducing the neighborhood size or analyzing subsets of gene programs to improve computational efficiency.

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L914-L926)

### Memory Management

The implementation includes explicit memory management to handle large intermediate arrays. After computing source and target scores, the function deletes these intermediate arrays to free memory before proceeding to aggregation steps. The communication strength matrices are stored in sparse CSR format throughout the pipeline to minimize memory overhead.

For datasets with more than approximately 100,000 cells, users should monitor memory usage and consider processing gene programs in batches if memory limitations are encountered. The aggregation step produces dense cell-type × cell-type matrices, which are typically much smaller than the cell-level matrices and therefore pose minimal memory constraints.

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L976-L988)

> [!TIP]
> The communication network computation caches spatial KNN graphs in `model.adata.uns['spatial_cci']` to avoid redundant computation. When analyzing multiple gene programs with the same neighborhood size, this optimization significantly reduces computation time. If you change the `n_neighbors` parameter, a new graph will be computed and cached, overwriting the previous cache.

## Biological Interpretation Guidelines

### Interpreting Communication Strengths

Communication strength values in the output DataFrame represent normalized measures of the intensity of signaling between cell type or niche pairs for a given gene program. However, these values should be interpreted with several considerations: (1) strengths are relative and comparable only within the same gene program and sample context; (2) the normalization is applied per gene program, so strengths cannot be directly compared across different gene programs; and (3) the absolute magnitude depends on experimental factors including sequencing depth, spatial resolution, and gene program prior selection.

For biological interpretation, focus on the relative ranking of communication edges within each gene program rather than absolute strength values. Strong communication edges typically indicate spatially co-localized cell populations with complementary expression of signaling molecules and receptors for the pathway of interest.

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L995-L1004)

### Validating Communication Networks

Validation of inferred communication networks should integrate multiple lines of evidence: (1) spatial colocalization of source and target cell populations in the tissue; (2) expression of known ligand-receptor pairs for the pathway; (3) consistency with known biology from literature and pathway databases; and (4) experimental perturbation results when available.

The NicheCompass framework facilitates validation through integration with spatial visualization tools. Users can overlay communication edge information on spatial coordinates using the spatial gene expression visualization capabilities to visually confirm that predicted communication occurs between spatially adjacent cell populations.

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L1014-L1148)

### Integration with External Knowledge

Communication network predictions can be enriched by integrating with external knowledge sources including known ligand-receptor interaction databases (e.g., CellPhoneDB, NicheNet, OmniPath), pathway annotations (e.g., KEGG, Reactome), and literature-curated interaction databases. This integration helps distinguish between novel predictions and validation of known interactions.

The framework provides utility functions for extracting gene programs from external interaction databases, enabling users to incorporate prior knowledge into the communication analysis. For example, users can create gene programs representing specific ligand-receptor signaling axes and then analyze communication patterns for these programs.

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L105-L211), [mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb#L1-L100)

## Next Steps

After computing communication networks, several downstream analyses can provide additional insights:

- **[Niche Characterization and Gene Importance Computation](25-niche-characterization-and-gene-importance-computation)**: Extend communication analysis to identify key genes and pathways driving niche-specific communication patterns
- **[Differential Gene Program Testing](23-differential-gene-program-testing)**: Identify gene programs with significantly different activity across conditions, which can explain altered communication patterns
- **[Latent Representation Extraction and Visualization](22-latent-representation-extraction-and-visualization)**: Visualize spatial patterns of gene program activity that underlie communication networks
- **[Single-Sample Niche Identification](19-single-sample-niche-identification)**: Identify spatially coherent cellular niches that serve as communication units

These analyses collectively provide a comprehensive understanding of cellular communication in spatial tissue contexts, from individual gene programs to tissue-level organization.

# Niche Characterization and Gene Importance Computation



This page provides comprehensive documentation on NicheCompass's advanced analytical capabilities for characterizing spatial niches and computing gene importance scores within gene programs. These features enable researchers to identify functionally distinct tissue microenvironments, understand cell-cell communication patterns, and determine which genes drive specific biological processes within identified niches.

## Overview of Niche Characterization Framework

Niche characterization in NicheCompass leverages the learned gene program representations to identify and analyze spatially coherent cell communities. The framework operates through a hierarchical process where latent gene program scores are aggregated across spatial neighborhoods, enabling the identification of functionally distinct niches based on shared gene program activity patterns. This approach transforms high-dimensional gene expression data into interpretable spatial maps of biological function, allowing researchers to identify microenvironments characterized by specific cellular activities and communication patterns.

The core insight driving this framework is that cells within the same spatial niche should exhibit coordinated activation of gene programs related to their shared functional context. By analyzing the spatial distribution of gene program scores and computing cell-cell communication potentials, NicheCompass can construct comprehensive networks of niche interactions and identify the key molecular players driving these spatially organized biological processes.

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L1-L4), [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L2-L4)

```mermaid
graph TB
    A[Trained NicheCompass Model] --> B[Latent GP Scores]
    A --> C[Spatial Connectivity Graph]
    B --> D[Cell-Cell Communication Potential Computation]
    C --> D
    D --> E[Niche Aggregation]
    E --> F[Communication GP Network]
    B --> G[Differential GP Testing]
    G --> H[Enriched GP Identification]
    F --> I[Niche Characterization]
    H --> I
    A --> J[Gene Importance Computation]
    J --> I
```

## Cell-Cell Communication Network Analysis

The foundation of niche characterization lies in computing gene program-specific communication networks between cells. This process quantifies the potential for communication between cell pairs based on coordinated gene program activity and spatial proximity. The `compute_communication_gp_network()` function implements this by first calculating source and target scores for each gene program, then aggregating these scores across spatial neighborhoods to determine cell-pair communication strengths.

The communication potential for a specific gene program is computed by considering three key components: the normalized expression levels of source and target genes associated with that gene program, the learned weights connecting those genes to the gene program in the decoder networks, and the spatial proximity between cells as defined by the neighborhood graph. This approach ensures that communication scores reflect both the molecular capacity for communication (gene expression and pathway connectivity) and the physical possibility of interaction (spatial adjacency).

Sources: [analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py#L871-L1013)

**Table: Communication Network Computation Components**

| Component | Description | Data Source | Purpose |
|-----------|-------------|-------------|---------|
| Source Gene Scores | Normalized expression × GP source weights × GP activity | `adata.X`, decoder weights | Quantify signaling capacity from source cells |
| Target Gene Scores | Normalized expression × GP target weights × GP activity | `adata.X`, decoder weights | Quantify receptor capacity in target cells |
| Spatial Neighborhood | KNN graph on spatial coordinates | `adata.obsm['spatial']` | Define physically possible interactions |
| Aggregation | Cell-type/group level averaging of cell-pair scores | `adata.obs[group_key]` | Generate interpretable niche-level networks |

The computation pipeline begins by constructing a k-nearest neighbor graph based on spatial coordinates, which defines the physical neighborhoods within which communication can occur. For each gene program, the algorithm retrieves the latent activity scores across all cells and identifies the source and target genes associated with that program through the decoder masks. Source and target scores are computed by combining normalized gene expression, the decoder weights connecting each gene to the gene program, and the gene program's latent activity score for each cell.

These scores are then averaged across all source and target genes for each cell to produce aggregate source and target scores per cell. The cell-pair communication strength is computed as the outer product of these aggregate scores, filtered through the spatial neighborhood graph to ensure only physically adjacent cells are considered. Finally, these cell-pair scores are aggregated across user-defined cell type or niche categories, normalized to the [0,1] range, and returned as a structured DataFrame suitable for network analysis and visualization.

> [!TIP]
> The communication network computation is computationally intensive for large datasets. The function caches the spatial neighborhood graph if the same `n_neighbors` parameter is used, but for different neighborhood sizes, recomputing the graph adds significant overhead. Consider standardizing on a single neighborhood size for multiple analyses.

## Differential Gene Program Testing for Niche Identification

Niche identification often requires identifying which gene programs are specifically enriched in particular spatial regions or cell groups compared to their surroundings or other reference populations. The `run_differential_gp_tests()` function implements a statistical framework for detecting gene programs that show significantly different activity between user-defined categories, such as spatial niches versus the rest of the tissue or one niche type versus another.

This method employs a Bayesian hypothesis testing approach comparing two hypotheses: the null hypothesis (h0) that gene program scores are higher in the category of interest versus the alternative hypothesis (h1) that scores are equal or higher in the comparison group. The evidence for each hypothesis is quantified using log Bayes factors, which provide a principled measure of enrichment that accounts for both the magnitude and variability of gene program scores across groups.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L830-L1052)

**Table: Differential GP Testing Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `cat_key` | str | required | Key in `adata.obs` defining categories for comparison |
| `selected_cats` | str/list | all categories | Categories to test for GP enrichment |
| `comparison_cats` | str/list | "rest" | Reference group ("rest" for all other categories) |
| `selected_gps` | str/list | all active GPs | Gene programs to test (None for all active) |
| `n_sample` | int | 10000 | Observations to sample per group for statistical testing |
| `log_bayes_factor_thresh` | float | 2.3 | Threshold for considering a GP enriched |
| `key_added` | str | "nichecompass_differential_gp_test_results" | Storage key for results |

The statistical implementation begins by retrieving latent representations (mean and standard deviation) for all cells, which are derived from the variational gene program autoencoder. For each gene program being tested, the method compares distributions between the category of interest and the comparison category by sampling equal numbers of observations from each group (default: 10,000 samples). The log Bayes factor is computed using the difference in mean scores normalized by the combined variance, following an adapted implementation from the scArches project.

Results are stored as a DataFrame in `adata.uns[key_added]` containing columns for category, gene program name, probabilities for each hypothesis (p_h0, p_h1), and the log Bayes factor. Gene programs exceeding the log Bayes factor threshold are considered enriched, and the normalized scores of enriched gene programs across all categories are added to `adata.obs` for visualization and downstream analysis. The method returns a list of all enriched gene programs across tested categories, providing a concise summary of the molecular signature distinguishing each niche or biological region.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L990-L1029)

## Gene Importance Computation

Understanding which genes drive specific gene program activity is crucial for biological interpretation and hypothesis generation. The `compute_gp_gene_importances()` function provides a quantitative assessment of each gene's contribution to a selected gene program by analyzing the learned decoder weights in the trained model. This analysis distinguishes between genes acting as communication sources (e.g., ligands, signaling molecules) and those acting as targets (e.g., receptors, response genes).

Gene importance scores are computed by normalizing the absolute weights connecting each gene to the gene program in the RNA decoder networks. The normalization is performed gene-wise across all cells, ensuring that importance scores reflect the relative contribution of each gene while accounting for differences in scale between different genes. This approach yields interpretable importance values that sum to 1.0 for each gene program, enabling direct comparison of the relative importance of different genes within the same program.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L1053-L1106)

**Table: Gene Importance DataFrame Structure**

| Column | Description | Data Type |
|--------|-------------|-----------|
| `gene` | Gene name | string |
| `gene_entity` | "source" or "target" indicating communication role | string |
| `gene_weight` | Raw decoder weight connecting gene to GP | float |
| `gene_importance` | Normalized importance score (sums to 1 per GP/entity) | float |

The importance computation retrieves the decoder weights for the specified gene program through `get_gp_data()`, which returns both source and target gene weights. These weights are normalized by their absolute sums to produce importance scores, with special handling for the case where all weights for a gene are zero (which would cause division by zero). The resulting DataFrame includes both raw weights and normalized importance scores, enabling researchers to understand both the magnitude and relative contribution of each gene.

For gene programs that include chromatin accessibility data (in multi-modal RNA+ATAC datasets), the analogous `compute_gp_peak_importances()` function provides the same analysis for peaks rather than genes, identifying which regulatory regions contribute most to each gene program's activity.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L1107-L1165)

> [!TIP]
> Gene importance scores can reveal unexpected biological insights. Genes with high importance but low expression may represent key regulators that exert outsized effects through low-abundance signaling molecules. Conversely, highly expressed genes with low importance may represent downstream effects rather than drivers of the gene program activity.

## Comprehensive Gene Program Summaries

For a holistic view of all gene programs and their associated genes, the `get_gp_summary()` function generates a comprehensive DataFrame containing information about every gene program, including its active status, constituent genes with weights and importances, and statistical metrics about program composition. This summary is particularly useful for exploratory analysis, quality assessment, and generating publication-ready tables of gene program annotations.

The summary includes separate information for source and target genes (and peaks for multi-modal models), with genes sorted by their absolute weights within each entity type. This organization enables quick identification of the most important genes for each communication direction. The summary also includes counts of total genes and non-zero genes per entity type, providing metrics of gene program sparsity and complexity.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L1689-L1965)

**Table: Gene Program Summary DataFrame Columns**

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `gp_name` | Gene program name |
| `all_gp_idx` | Index among all gene programs (including inactive) |
| `gp_active` | Boolean indicating if GP is active in model |
| `active_gp_idx` | Index among active gene programs (Int64, NA if inactive) |
| `n_source_genes` | Total number of source genes associated with GP |
| `n_non_zero_source_genes` | Source genes with non-zero decoder weights |
| `n_target_genes` | Total number of target genes associated with GP |
| `n_non_zero_target_genes` | Target genes with non-zero decoder weights |
| `gp_source_genes` | List of source gene names, sorted by weight |
| `gp_target_genes` | List of target gene names, sorted by weight |
| `gp_source_genes_weights` | Corresponding source gene decoder weights |
| `gp_target_genes_weights` | Corresponding target gene decoder weights |
| `gp_source_genes_importances` | Normalized importance scores for source genes |
| `gp_target_genes_importances` | Normalized importance scores for target genes |

For models trained on multi-modal data, additional columns are included for peak information, following the same structure as gene columns but with regulatory region identifiers instead of gene names. The summary includes handling for "addon" gene programs that may have been learned de novo during training rather than being specified from prior knowledge, ensuring complete coverage of all programs in the model.

## Neighbor Importance and Spatial Context

Beyond gene-centric analysis, understanding the spatial context of each cell's latent representation is crucial for niche characterization. The `get_neighbor_importances()` function retrieves the aggregation weights learned by the node label aggregator, which quantify how much importance each cell attributes to its neighboring cells during the reconstruction process. These weights represent a learned measure of spatial influence that reflects the model's understanding of which neighbors are most relevant for predicting a cell's molecular profile.

The neighbor importance matrix is sparse (n_obs × n_obs), where each row represents a cell and the non-zero entries in that row indicate the aggregation weights for that cell's neighbors. This matrix is not symmetric—cell A may attribute high importance to cell B, but cell B may attribute lower importance to cell A, reflecting directional influence patterns rather than reciprocal relationships.

Sources: [nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py#L1599-L1688)

The implementation processes the entire dataset in batches through the node label aggregator, retrieving the attention coefficients or aggregation weights for each cell-neighbor pair. When using the "one-hop-attention" node label method, the mean across attention heads is computed to produce a single importance score per edge. The global edge index is used to map batch-local indices back to the global cell indices, and the aggregation weights are assembled into a sparse matrix in CSR format for efficient storage and subsequent analysis.
